findings.title: sum_ret/sum_sq/days_in_market omit every entry-cost day, so the expectancy + Sharpe gates that release real money are computed on an upward-biased subset of the booked return series
findings.what_breaks: The accumulator is gated on YESTERDAY's positions: `if s["positions"]: s["days_in_market"] += 1; s["sum_ret"] += net; s["sum_sq"] += net*net`. On any day the contestant was flat and re-entered, day_ret is 0 and `net` is pure entry cost (negative) -- that net IS multiplied into s["equity"] (line 797) and IS appended to s["history"] (line 806), but never enters sum_ret/sum_sq/days_in_market. Exit days ARE counted (positions non-empty), so the omission is one-directional: upward. report() line 1212 then computes `mean = s["sum_ret"] / max(s["days_in_market"],1)` and the Sharpe from sum_sq, and hands both to promotion_check as the checks labelled "expectancy (mean daily net return)" and "sharpe" -- the two gates that move a contestant up LADDER toward real capital. Neither is the mean/variance of the daily net returns the engine actually booked. It is also a contradiction inside one function: promotion_check's "excess return vs benchmark" rows come from excess_return_stats(s["history"], ...), which uses EVERY history row, so two gates in the same checks list are computed on two different return series. The same biased mean feeds propose_evolutions (line 920) and update_advisor_trust (line 1039). Separate manifestation, same guard: for fn=="cash" (line 771) positions are always {} (sig_cash returns {}), so a cash contestant's sum_ret stays 0.0 and days_in_market stays 0 forever.
findings.failing_input: Pure-Python replication of lines 768-806 + round_trip_cost (VARIABLE_COST_PER_SIDE=0.00111, DP_CHARGE_PER_SCRIP=15.34, LADDER[1]=25000): a 2-ticker 50/50 strategy invested on days 0-1 of every 4-day cycle, market +0.170%/day while invested, 130 days. Result: days_on_rung=130 (bar 126), trades=65 (bar 10), drawdown -0.16% (bar -12%), reported mean=+0.0005494 (bar 0.0005), reported Sharpe=7.46 (bar 0.4) -- EVERY numeric RULES gate passes -- while equity ends at 0.99901, i.e. the contestant LOST money. 0.0333 of entry-cost drag was omitted from sum_ret. Live-ledger confirmation (factory_state/ledger.json, read-only): event_infra_t20 has sum_ret=+0.010300 with days_in_market=5 -> reported expectancy +0.002060 = 4.1x min_expectancy, while the sum of its own 31 history nets is +0.003170 and equity is 0.99644; the gap +0.007128 is exactly the two excluded entry days of -0.003564 (2026-09-15, 2026-09-29). input_cost_crude_cement: sum_ret=0.0, days_in_market=0 -> reported expectancy exactly 0.0, yet its history carries -0.001110 of real cost. crypto_cash_baseline (fn="cash", profiles/crypto.json cash_rate_annual=0.0525): reported expectancy is exactly 0.0 and Sharpe NaN permanently while equity compounds at 5.25%/yr, so the designated B0 "cash baseline" can never be compared on the metric it exists to be the bar for.
findings.fix: Accumulate sum_ret/sum_sq on every day the engine books a net -- unconditionally, next to the history.append -- and keep days_in_market as a separate exposure counter rather than reusing it as the divisor (report() line 1211 must divide by the count of days summed, not by exposure days). If the metric is deliberately meant to be per-exposure-day, then the entry cost must be charged on the first exposed day instead of the flat day, and the fn=="cash" accrual branch must mark the day as in-market. Either way the divisor has to match the set of days summed, and promotion_check's "expectancy (mean daily net return)" label should name whichever series it actually is.
findings.status: VERIFIED-IN-PART 2026-10-11 (see bug_log: entry-day cost omitted from sum_ret/sum_sq; replica shows a pass-but-lost-money band)

findings.title: sig_event_drift returns negative weights and update() books the resulting short basket, contradicting 00_DESIGN.md's verbatim "No leverage, no shorting ... in any class, ever" -- already recorded on 10 days in the live ledger
findings.what_breaks: `d = float(np.sign(hit.iloc[-1]))` is -1.0 whenever the leader's triggering move was DOWN, and line 278 returns `{t: d / len(lags) for t in lags}` -- i.e. weight -1/len(lags) on every lag, a short basket. update() books it with no long-only guard: day_ret = sum(w * ret) profits when those names fall, and tickers_sold (line 793) counts a short OPEN as a sell-day and levies a Rs 15.34/scrip DP charge. docs/capital_engine/00_DESIGN.md Section 3 item 5 states verbatim: "**No leverage, no shorting, no margin beyond collateral held**, in any class, ever, by construction in the signal functions (hard rule)." Section 2's class table defines sleeve A2 as "the existing NSE equity arena (`factory.py`, capital earned via `LADDER`)", so the arena is explicitly in scope. sig_trend_long_flat's own docstring (line 376) commits to "Never short, never leveraged" and sig_fixed_weight's to "Long-only, unlevered" -- event_drift is the only family that does not honour it. A short in NSE cash-delivery equity is not reachable without intraday square-off, SLB or F&O (which CLAUDE.md's hard rules forbid adding), so the P&L booked on those days is not achievable under the model the project claims to be paper-trading, yet it feeds equity, Sharpe and the promotion gate. The DP charge on a short open is additionally a wrong cost number on its own terms: an infra short open is charged 0.003564 against 0.001110 for an identical-turnover long open.
findings.failing_input: Already in the live ledger (factory_state/ledger.json, read-only) -- 10 short-entry days across 4 contestants: event_cement_t17 (2026-09-07, 2026-09-15, 2026-09-29), event_infra_t20 (2026-09-15, 2026-09-29), event_steel_t22 (2026-09-14, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-02), event_steel_t30 (2026-09-28, 2026-10-02). Identified by the arithmetically unique entry-day net: for infra (UNIVERSE['infra'] = 5 names, leader LT.NS, so 4 lags) a LONG open from flat gives turn=1.0, tickers_sold=0 -> cost 1.0*0.00111 = 0.001110; a SHORT open gives turn=1.0, tickers_sold=4 -> cost 0.00111 + 4*15.34/25000 = 0.003564. The ledger records net = -0.003564 on exactly those dates (and -0.001110 on 2026-10-01, a long open). Minimal synthetic repro: any px panel whose leader has a move < -p['threshold'] in its last p['hold'] rows -> sig_event_drift returns {lag: -0.25, ...}.
findings.fix: Clamp sig_event_drift to long-or-flat -- return {} when d < 0 (or use max(d, 0.0)) -- matching sig_trend_long_flat and sig_fixed_weight. If shorting is genuinely intended for A2, that is a design-doc change plus Het's fresh in-session authorization, not code that silently contradicts 00_DESIGN.md Section 3 item 5. Independently, tickers_sold (line 793) should count only reductions of a POSITIVE holding, so opening a short is never charged a demat DP fee.

findings.title: day_ret has no presence/NaN guard: a held ticker missing from the panel silently books 0.00% forever, and a NaN return poisons equity permanently and freezes the verdict at "hold"
findings.what_breaks: `day_ret = sum(w * todays_ret.get(t, 0.0) for t, w in s["positions"].items())` has neither a px.columns check nor an isna check. (a) Ticker absent from the panel -> the dict default silently books 0.00% for that sleeve every day, while turnover cost on it is still charged at line 795, and nothing is printed; append_market_log's `if not pd.isna(px[t].iloc[-1])` filter also silently drops it, so the condition surfaces nowhere. (b) Ticker present but NaN at `sel` -- fetch_prices' `.ffill()` cannot repair a column with no valid value in the window (an all-NaN column for a renamed/failed symbol) -- -> day_ret is NaN, net is NaN, `s["equity"] *= (1 + net)` makes equity NaN permanently; `s["peak"] = max(s["peak"], s["equity"])` keeps the old peak because max(1.0, nan) returns 1.0, so dd is NaN, `dd < R["max_drawdown"]` (report line 1223) is False -> never DEMOTE, promotion_check's `not _isnan(have)` rejects it -> never PROMOTE, and the contestant is frozen at verdict "hold" with NaN sum_ret/sum_sq forever; json.dump then writes bare `NaN` tokens into ledger.json, which is not valid JSON per RFC 8259. The inconsistency is quotable in-file: sig_benchmark checks `if BENCHMARK in px.columns`, sig_fixed_weight's docstring commits to "Tickers missing from the price panel are dropped and the rest are renormalised to gross 1.0", and fixed_weight_next documents "NaN = 0" -- but sig_event_drift (line 277), sig_input_cost (~289) and sig_monsoon (~302) all return every ticker in UNIVERSE[sector] with no presence or isna filter, and update() adds none of its own.
findings.failing_input: (a) s['positions'] = {'LT.NS':0.0, 'IRB.NS':0.25, 'KNRCON.NS':0.25, 'PNCINFRA.NS':0.25, 'HGINFRA.NS':0.25} with HGINFRA.NS absent from px.columns -> day_ret = 0.75 * basket return instead of 1.0 x, with no warning (dict.get default verified). (b) Same positions with px['HGINFRA.NS'] all-NaN: verified in python3 -- 1.0*(1+nan) = nan; max(1.0, nan) = 1.0; nan/1.0-1 = nan; (nan < -0.12) is False; json.dumps({'history':[['2026-10-09',nan,nan]]}) emits '{"history": [["2026-10-09", NaN, NaN]]}', and a strict parser rejects the bare NaN token.
findings.fix: Drop and renormalise unavailable tickers inside sig_event_drift / sig_input_cost / sig_monsoon the way sig_fixed_weight already documents, and make update() fail loudly rather than silently: read `r = todays_ret.get(t)` and, if it is None or pd.isna(r), print a warning and skip the day (or that contestant) instead of multiplying NaN into equity -- the same fail-loudly posture lines 710-715 already take for an empty download.

findings.title: Promotion-gate expectancy and Sharpe are computed over a different, cost-incomplete sample than equity: every re-entry day's transaction cost is charged to equity but excluded from sum_ret/sum_sq
findings.what_breaks: update() lines 796-806 charge the full turnover cost into equity (`net = day_ret - round_trip_cost(...)`; `s["equity"] *= (1 + net)`) and append `net` to `history` on EVERY day, but accumulate `sum_ret`/`sum_sq`/`days_in_market` only inside `if s["positions"]:` -- and that test reads YESTERDAY's positions, before line 805 assigns today's. So on any day the contestant re-enters from flat, `day_ret` is 0 and `net` is pure cost, equity pays it, and the statistics never see it. report() then computes `mean = s["sum_ret"] / max(s["days_in_market"],1)` (line 1211-1212) and feeds it to promotion_check() as the gate's `("expectancy (mean daily net return)", mean, R["min_expectancy"])` check (line 1157). Two wrong numbers result: (a) the gate's expectancy omits the entry leg of every round trip -- roughly half of all transaction cost for any strategy that cycles to flat; (b) because flat days are dropped from the sample entirely, `mean` and `var` are conditional on being in the market while being treated as per-trading-day figures and annualized by sqrt(252), inflating Sharpe by 1/sqrt(days_in_market/rows). This contradicts three committed statements: the gate's own label says "mean daily NET return"; the PAPER_HOLDING_TAX_WEEKLY comment asserts `RULES["min_expectancy"] (~12.6%/yr)`, which only holds at 252 in-market days per year; and tools/analyze_q4_vs_benchmark.py:102 prints this exact quantity as "mean daily return (net of cost)". It is also internally inconsistent inside one promotion_check() call: the beat-the-benchmark leg uses `excess_return_stats(s["history"], ...)`, i.e. the cost-complete, all-days series, while the raw expectancy/sharpe legs use the conditional sum_ret sample.
findings.failing_input: Live ledger factory_state/ledger.json, contestant `input_cost_lag` (days_on_rung=70, rows=70, days_in_market=7, trades=4, sum_ret=+0.00751, sum(history)=+0.00450). report() computes mean = 0.00751/7 = +0.00107330, which PASSES min_expectancy=0.0005 by 2.1x. The cost-complete mean over the same 70 recorded days is 0.00450/70 = +0.00006433, which FAILS the same bar by 7.8x. Omitted entry cost = sum_ret - sum(history) = +0.003010 (= 0.000430 per in-market day). Sharpe is scaled by 1/sqrt(7/70) = 3.16x. Same pattern, every traded contestant: event_cement_t17 omits +0.014374 (= 0.001106/in-market day, i.e. 2.2x the whole 0.0005 bar) with 1.54x Sharpe inflation; event_steel_t22 omits +0.006281 with 1.44x; input_cost_crude_cement records sum_ret=0.0 and days_in_market=0 while its history sums to -0.00111, exactly one entry leg (turn=1.0 x VARIABLE_COST_PER_SIDE=0.00111) that equity paid and the statistics discarded.
findings.fix: Accumulate the statistics over the same sample as `history`/`equity`: move `s["sum_ret"] += net` and `s["sum_sq"] += net*net` out of the `if s["positions"]:` block so they run on every recorded day, and divide by the recorded-day count rather than `days_in_market` in report()/judge.py/dashboard.py (keep `days_in_market` as its own counter for post_tax_expectancy's holding-period classification, which genuinely wants in-market days). This changes what the promotion gate reads, so under CLAUDE.md it needs Het's fresh, explicit, in-session authorization before any edit -- and note it only ever makes the bar harder, like the 2026-08-30 Q5 fix. Recomputing the existing aggregates from each contestant's stored `history` would also repair the already-distorted live values, which is the same decision as ACCELERATION_PLAN STEP 6.

findings.title: Signal functions get the untruncated price panel including the trailing phantom row, so Brent-driven contestants see post-NSE-close data (breaking the stated "no lookahead") and event_drift's hold window is silently one session short
findings.what_breaks: The phantom-day guard selects `sel` (the last real row) and books P&L from `rets.loc[sel]`, and line 761 correctly truncates the panel for the market log: `append_market_log(today, px.loc[:sel])`. But line 773 passes the FULL `px` to the signal functions: `targets = IMPLS[params["fn"]](px, params)`. Since the guard went live the trailing phantom row is the normal daily case, not an edge case (bug_log.md / EVIDENCE/CE-0-04.md, run 37671669431: `PHANTOM SKIPPED: 2026-10-07 (100% unchanged)` then `Arena updated 2026-10-06`). Two concrete consequences. (a) LOOKAHEAD: MACRO_PROXIES are deliberately excluded from the phantom test precisely because Brent trades when NSE does not, so on that extra row BZ=F carries a REAL new close while every NSE column is a forward-filled duplicate. `sig_input_cost` (line 287, `c = px[p["proxy"]].iloc[-p["lb"]:]`) therefore decides today's positions using Brent's close for session sel+1 -- and on the next run those exact positions are what session sel+1's NSE return is booked against (line 768). ICE Brent settles ~19:30 GMT, hours after the 15:30 IST NSE close, so the position credited with trading a session was chosen with information published after that session ended. Line 766 states the opposite invariant verbatim: `# P&L from positions decided yesterday (no lookahead)`. (b) WRONG WINDOW: `sig_event_drift` line 272 (`recent = lead.iloc[-p["hold"]:]`) counts the phantom row as one of the `hold` days. Its leader is an NSE ticker, forward-filled, so its pct_change on that row is exactly 0.0 and can never satisfy `abs(recent) > threshold`. The documented 3-day event window is therefore 2 real sessions for all nine live `event_*` contestants, and 1 session in a week with a holiday plus an unposted session. `sig_momentum` (line 282) and the SMA branch of `sig_trend_long_flat` have their lookback windows shifted/double-weighted by the same row.
findings.failing_input: FACTORY_PROFILE=equity_nse, panel ending [..., D-1(real), D(real), D+1(phantom: all NSE forward-filled, BZ=F real)] -- the shape run 37671669431 actually produced. sel=D. (a) `input_cost_crude_cement` / `input_cost_crude_steel` (proxy BZ=F, lb=20, drop=-0.05): the 20-day Brent window ends at D+1, so the decision to hold the 7-name cement basket uses Brent's D+1 close; the next run books D+1's cement returns against that basket. (b) `event_cement_t17` (threshold=0.017, hold=3): with ULTRACEMCO.NS returns of +0.000 at D+1 (forward-filled), -0.005 at D, +0.025 at D-1, `lead.iloc[-3:]` = [D-1, D, D+1] still sees the hit at D-1, but one session later that hit has fallen out of the window while the design says it should still be inside a 3-day hold -- the position exits a day early, every time.
findings.fix: Pass the same truncated panel the market log already gets: `targets = IMPLS[params["fn"]](px.loc[:sel], params)` at line 773 (and use `px.loc[:sel]` for the `fixed_weight`/`trend_long_flat` branches below it). That makes the signal input and the booked return share one as-of date, removes the macro-proxy lookahead, and restores `hold`/`lookback` to real sessions. Behaviour-affecting on the promotion gate's data, so it belongs in a reviewed change with a regression test built on the existing tests/test_phantom_guard.py panel, not a quick edit.

findings.title: No NaN or missing-ticker guard in the daily write path: one dataless ticker either NaN-poisons a contestant's equity forever (and it then never demotes or retires) or silently liquidates it while the promotion clock keeps running
findings.what_breaks: `day_ret = sum(w * todays_ret.get(t, 0.0) for t, w in s["positions"].items())` relies on `.get`'s default, but Series.get only returns the default when the KEY IS ABSENT -- for a ticker that is a column with no data (all-NaN after `dropna(how="all").ffill()`, since ffill cannot fill a column with no first valid value) it returns the stored NaN. `sig_event_drift` (line 278) and `sig_input_cost` (line 290) build their weight dicts straight from `UNIVERSE[p["sector"]]` with no `px.columns` or NaN filter, unlike `sig_fixed_weight` (line 329, `if t in px.columns and ... not pd.isna(px[t].iloc[-1])`) and `sig_trend_long_flat` (line 391), and unlike `fixed_weight_next` (line 359, `0.0 if pd.isna(r) else float(r)`), which guards the very same `todays_ret` object one line below the unguarded `day_ret`. One NaN makes `net` NaN, so `s["equity"] *= (1 + net)` is NaN permanently, `sum_ret`/`sum_sq` are NaN, and `NaN` tokens are written into ledger.json -- accepted by Python's json but invalid RFC-8259, so any JS `JSON.parse` consumer of the published state throws. Worse, the contestant then never exits: `dd = s["equity"]/s["peak"] - 1` is NaN, `nan < R["max_drawdown"]` is False, so report() never DEMOTEs it, it never accrues paper_failures, never retires, and keeps `retired: False` -- which keeps it inside report()'s `n_tests` count, permanently raising the multiplicity Sharpe floor (`sqrt(252/n)` scaled by `inv_cdf(1 - alpha/n_tests)`) for every honest contestant. In the other branch -- the column genuinely dropped, which the repo's own tools/diagnose_nifty100_tickers.py:10 asserts is what happens ("A wrong/delisted ticker doesn't crash the pipeline (fetch_prices just drops it from the panel)") -- `sig_momentum`'s `px[names]` (line 282) raises KeyError, and line 774's bare `except Exception` converts that into `targets = {}`: `mom_nifty100_lb90` pays one full exit cost, sits flat forever, and `s["days_on_rung"] += 1` (line 799) keeps advancing its 126-day clock, with nothing but a `[warn]` line in an Actions log. No health_check check covers either case (check_stale_ledger, check_duplicate_dates, check_registry_drift, check_phantom_days, check_kill_switch -- none inspects equity/net for NaN or a contestant stalled flat).
findings.failing_input: FACTORY_PROFILE=equity_nse with any one of UNIVERSE["cement"] = ['ULTRACEMCO.NS','AMBUJACEM.NS','ACC.NS','SHREECEM.NS','JKCEMENT.NS','RAMCOCEM.NS','DALBHARAT.NS'] returned by yfinance as an all-NaN column (a renamed/delisted symbol -- the repo already documents Yahoo NSE holes in docs/capital_engine/research/R4_shield_tickers_check.md and bug_log.md's 2026-10-08 note). `sig_input_cost` returns {t: 1/7 for all seven}, so with the other six at +0.01/+0.02/etc.: day_ret = 0.25*nan + ... = nan, net = nan, equity = 1.0*(1+nan) = nan, peak stays 1.0 (max(1.0, nan) returns 1.0), dd = nan, `dd < -0.12` is False -> no DEMOTE, ever. History row serializes as ["2026-10-06", NaN, NaN] (verified: json.dumps gives the bare token `NaN`). With the column dropped instead, `px[UNIVERSE["nifty100"]]` raises KeyError, line 774 swallows it, and mom_nifty100_lb90 goes flat permanently.
findings.fix: Mirror the guard that already exists at line 359: compute `r = todays_ret.get(t); r = 0.0 if r is None or pd.isna(r) else float(r)` in the day_ret sum, and add the `t in px.columns and not pd.isna(...)` filter that sig_fixed_weight uses to sig_event_drift and sig_input_cost. Separately, narrow line 774's bare `except Exception`: a KeyError on the universe is a data-integrity failure, not a 'no signal today' -- it should hold existing positions and surface a hard error (or a health_check finding) rather than liquidating silently while days_on_rung advances. A ledger-level NaN check in tools/health_check.py would catch the whole class cheaply and for free.

findings.title: Promotion gate's "expectancy (mean daily net return)" is computed over days_in_market, not booked sessions — every position-entry day's cost is charged to equity but censored from sum_ret, flipping the sign of the gate metric
findings.what_breaks:
In update(), the statistics behind the promotion gate are accrued only inside `if s["positions"]:` (line 801) — i.e. only on days the contestant already held a position *coming into* the day:

    801:        if s["positions"]:
    802:            s["days_in_market"] += 1
    803:            s["sum_ret"] += net
    804:            s["sum_sq"] += net * net

But `net` on line 800 is charged to `equity` and appended to `history` on EVERY booked session (line 806). On a position-entry day yesterday's positions are `{}`, so `day_ret` is 0 and `net` is exactly minus the entry turnover cost — that cost hits equity and history and is then dropped from sum_ret/sum_sq/days_in_market. report() then does:

    1211:        n = max(s["days_in_market"], 1)
    1212:        mean = s["sum_ret"] / n
    1217:            sharpe = mean / np.sqrt(var) * np.sqrt(252)

and promotion_check hands that number to the gate under the label it prints verbatim to a human (judge.py renders these):

    1157:        ("expectancy (mean daily net return)", mean, R["min_expectancy"]),

It is not the mean daily net return. Two compounding errors: (a) exit-leg costs are included while entry-leg costs are not, so roughly half of every round trip's variable cost is invisible to the gate; (b) a per-day-of-exposure average is compared against an absolute per-calendar-day bar, and annualised by sqrt(252) as if exposure were 252 days/yr.

CONTRADICTIONS (quotable):
1. advisors.py:77 — backtest()'s docstring: "Walk the full history exactly like update() does: yesterday's target positions realize P&L against today's return, costs charged on turnover." advisors.py:107 is `daily_net.append(net)` with NO `if positions:` filter, and its sharpe() averages over all days. The parameter bank that report()'s evolution step blends into live contestants is therefore scored on a per-calendar-day, entry-cost-inclusive basis while the live gate uses a per-held-day, entry-cost-censored basis. One of the two docstrings is false.
2. docs/research/Q5_statistical_power.md: "min_expectancy = 0.0005/day. Under the null the sample mean has standard deviation 0.01119/sqrt(126) = 0.000997" and "sharpe >= 0.4 is equivalent to mean >= 0.4 x 0.01119 / sqrt(252) = 0.00028". The committed power calculation Het authorized the Q5 tightening against models n = 126 (the days_on_rung horizon) and 252 days/yr. The code never uses that n for either gate.
3. multiplicity_sharpe_floor docstring (line ~1110): "an annualised Sharpe estimated from n daily returns is approximately Normal(0, 252/n)" — yet it is fed `n_paired` from history (calendar sessions) while the raw `sharpe` it is meant to correct is built on days_in_market.

Blast radius beyond the verdict: the same censored `mean` drives propose_evolutions (line 920) and update_advisor_trust (line 1039), so the advisor trust_weight self-tunes on it too — and EXECUTION_PLAN.md 5(d) makes trust_weight decay a kill condition.

findings.title: Expectancy and Sharpe exclude every entry-day transaction cost, so report() can PROMOTE a contestant whose equity curve lost money
findings.line: 1211-1218 (report(), consumes the numbers) with root cause at 801-804 (update()); label at 1157
findings.what_breaks:
update() charges the full cost to equity (`s["equity"] *= (1 + net)`, line 795) on every day, but only records the day into the expectancy/Sharpe accumulators when the contestant was ALREADY holding at the open:

    s["equity"] *= (1 + net)
    ...
    if s["positions"]:            # <- yesterday's positions, EMPTY on an entry day
        s["days_in_market"] += 1
        s["sum_ret"] += net
        s["sum_sq"] += net * net
    s["positions"] = targets

On a day the contestant goes flat -> long, `s["positions"]` is `{}`, so `net` (which is exactly `-round_trip_cost(buy_leg)`) is charged to equity and then dropped from both the numerator and the denominator. The EXIT day is counted (positions non-empty, net includes the sell-side variable cost plus every DP charge). The asymmetry biases the number upward.

report() then computes the PROMOTE inputs from those accumulators (`n = max(s["days_in_market"], 1)`, `mean = s["sum_ret"] / n`, `var = s["sum_sq"]/n - mean**2`) and hands `mean` to promotion_check() under the label "expectancy (mean daily net return)" (line 1157) against RULES["min_expectancy"]. Note the internal inconsistency inside promotion_check() itself: the beat-the-benchmark gate reads `s["history"]` row[1], which DOES contain every entry day, so the Q5 excess-return gate is cost-complete while the expectancy and Sharpe gates are not.

This is visible right now in the committed ledger. It also contradicts a committed kill condition: EXECUTION_PLAN.md Section 5(c) lists "Promoted strategies systematically underperform their paper results once real costs apply -> The whole promotion methodology is invalid". findings.title: excess_return_stats() subtracts the benchmark 1:1 on days the contestant had NO exposure, so the index's own drift is credited as alpha — and the multiplicity floor is sized on calendar days, not exposure days

The effective regression coefficient on the benchmark is fixed at 1, so for a contestant with exposure beta != 1 the excess series is dominated by (beta-1)*market, not by skill: exposure 0 earns +market-drift-inverted, and sig_event_drift can take exposure -1 (line 276, `d = float(np.sign(...))` yields -1 for a down leader), which earns -2x the market. The live gate is not a one-look test. This is the number the whole RULES change is justified by (factory.py:131-147: "the gate above, on its own, hands a PROMOTE to a PURE-NOISE contestant ~85% of the time ... The two keys below are the fix Het chose"), and it is also what EXECUTION_PLAN Section 5a's 12-month kill condition leans on -- Q5 itself warned that a bar cleared by chance compromises the project's honest off-ramp. findings.title: Phantom-day guard covers P&L but not the signal call: positions are computed from a non-session row
findings.what_breaks: update() selects the last REAL row `sel = real_rows.index[-1]` (731), books P&L with `rets.loc[sel]` (733) and even truncates the market log to `px.loc[:sel]` (761) — but passes the UNTRUNCATED `px` to every signal function (773). So whenever the panel's final row is a phantom (an NSE holiday that exists only because BZ=F traded, or a not-yet-posted session) AND `sel` is not already recorded, every sig_* function treats the phantom row as "today": sig_momentum's `iloc[-lookback:]` window drops its oldest real session and adds the non-session, sig_input_cost reads `px[proxy].iloc[-1]` from it, sig_event_drift's `lead.iloc[-hold:]` loses one real day of its hold window, and sig_trend_long_flat compares `close.iloc[-1]` (the stale row) against a Donchian window that then includes the real session its own docstring calls "today". The repo's own measurement is 6 of 28 recorded days phantom (CE-0-04 header, run 37176894252).

findings.title: sig_event_drift / sig_input_cost assign weights to tickers never checked against the price panel — an all-NaN column permanently NaNs a contestant and emits invalid JSON

(A) If a universe ticker is in the panel but its column is entirely NaN — a renamed/delisted/404 ticker that the data source still returns as a column; this project has already had one (the factory.py header records TATAMOTORS.NS as a "real 404 on Yahoo", and bug_log.md's R4 note says "Yahoo's NSE daily series has holes that may never fill") — then update():768 `todays_ret.get(t, 0.0)` returns NaN (the key exists, the value is NaN), so day_ret is NaN, `s["equity"] *= (1+net)` makes equity NaN, and because NaN is absorbing, every subsequent day stays NaN forever. sum_ret/sum_sq are NaN too, so the contestant's whole track record is destroyed, and json.dump writes a bare `NaN` token into factory_state/ledger.json, which strict JSON parsers (JS JSON.parse, jq) reject — the ledger is the file dashboard.py and the Trading Floor tooling fetch. promotion_check()'s `_isnan` guard means it fails closed rather than promoting, so this destroys evidence silently instead of granting capital. findings.title: The min_expectancy promotion gate reads a mean that excludes every entry day, so entry transaction cost is charged to equity but not to the number that releases capital
findings.line: 801-804 (`if s["positions"]:` guards sum_ret/sum_sq/days_in_market), consumed at 1212-1213 and gated at 1157
findings.what_breaks: `sum_ret`/`sum_sq`/`days_in_market` are only incremented when YESTERDAY's positions were non-empty. On the day a flat contestant ENTERS, yesterday's positions are empty, so that day's `net` — which is pure entry cost (turn=1.0) — is multiplied into `equity` but never enters `sum_ret` or the denominator. The EXIT day is counted (yesterday was held), so exit cost IS included. `report()` then computes `mean = sum_ret / max(days_in_market, 1)` and promotion_check() compares it against `min_expectancy=0.0005` under the label "expectancy (mean daily net return)" (factory.py:1157) — a label that is false for any strategy that goes flat between trades. The bias is one-directional and fails OPEN on the gate whose entire job is withholding real money. It is also internally inconsistent inside a single promotion_check() call: `excess_return_stats()` averages over ALL paired history days while `mean`/`sharpe` average over the in-market subset only. Affects 15 of 27 live contestants (12 event_drift + 3 input_cost), i.e. every family that is flat between signals; rotating momentum contestants are unaffected because yesterday's positions are rarely empty.
findings.failing_input: Live ledger, read-only. event_infra_t20: 31 recorded days, days_in_market=5, sum_ret=+0.010301 -> reported expectancy +0.00206017, which PASSES the 0.0005 bar by 4.1x; sum of all 31 history nets = +0.003173 -> honest mean daily net return +0.00010235, which FAILS the bar by 5x. input_cost_lag: reported +0.00107330 (PASSES) vs honest +0.00006433 (FAILS by 16x). event_steel_t22's history contains days whose net is exactly -0.00111 (= 1.0 turnover x VARIABLE_COST_PER_SIDE, zero sells) on 2026-09-04, 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-23 — pure entry cost, none of it in sum_ret (sum of all nets -0.092840 vs stored sum_ret -0.086559). Either accumulate sum_ret/sum_sq/days_in_market on every day the contestant had positions OR traded (i.e. `if s["positions"] or turn > 0`), which captures the entry day and its cost, or keep the in-market denominator but relabel the check so it no longer claims to be the mean daily net return and subtract the uncounted entry cost before comparing. Changing the gate's input is an evidence decision (it moves every existing contestant's reported expectancy and the golden-master fingerprint), so it needs Het — queue it rather than acting. Note it in .autonomous/bug_log.md; the existing 'ledger-duplicate-trading-days' entry touches sum_ret but not this.

findings.title: A single all-NaN ticker column makes day_ret NaN, permanently poisoning equity/sum_ret/sum_sq and writing invalid JSON; the fixed_weight cash fallback guarantees it repeats every day of the outage
findings.line: 768 (day_ret), 350-353 (cash fail-closed), 359 (the guard that is missing above)
findings.what_breaks: factory.py:768-769 computes `day_ret = sum(w * todays_ret.get(t, 0.0) for t, w in s["positions"].items())`. `Series.get(t, 0.0)` returns the 0.0 default only when the KEY IS ABSENT; when the column exists but its value is NaN it returns NaN. `fetch_prices()` does `px.dropna(how="all").ffill()`, which cannot repair an all-NaN column (verified: ffill leaves it NaN, and the rows survive dropna because the other tickers have data), so `rets.loc[sel][t]` is NaN while `t` is still in the index. One such day gives day_ret=NaN -> net=NaN -> `s["equity"] *= (1 + net)` is NaN forever (multiplicative, no self-healing), `sum_ret`/`sum_sq` NaN forever (so Sharpe/expectancy/drawdown for that contestant are destroyed for the rest of the 126-day promotion clock), and `save_state()` writes bare `NaN` tokens into ledger.json, which is not valid JSON (Python's json reads it back; a strict parser / JSON.parse rejects it). The audited cash fallback at 350-353 turns this from a one-day hit into a certainty: when the cash sleeve's column vanishes it returns `dict(cur), dict(cur)`, deliberately KEEPING the vanished sleeve in `positions` ('rather than silently going 100% risk'), so every day of the outage re-poisons and the NaN-returning ticker is never shed. The correct guard already exists 9 lines below, inside the same helper, at line 359: `grown[t] = w * (1.0 + (0.0 if pd.isna(r) else float(r)))` -- the drift path is NaN-safe, the P&L path one screen above is not. Trigger is routine: a per-symbol failure inside a batch `yf.download` (yfinance returns the column all-NaN and logs an error), a renamed or delisted symbol (profiles/shield_nse.json's own `candidate_tickers_note` says all four tickers are CANDIDATES until verified), or a typo in a profile's `weights`.
findings.failing_input: shield_nse profile, tests/synthetic_panel.make_panel(seed=20261004, 300 history + 12 cycles), fetch_prices monkeypatched so exactly ONE download (cycle 5, 2026-10-12) returns `px["LIQUIDCASE.NS"] = np.nan`. Observed ledger shield_core history: ['2026-10-09', -0.003414, 0.9912] then ['2026-10-12', nan, nan], then SEVEN later days with perfectly finite net returns (-0.000225, 0.000976, -0.009678, -0.004235, 0.004174, -0.0002) all recorded against equity=nan. Final state: equity=nan, sum_ret=nan, sum_sq=nan, days_in_market=11, and `"NaN" in open("ledger.json").read()` is True / strict JSON parse raises on the non-standard constant. Identical outcome with GOLDBEES.NS instead of the cash sleeve. Minimal proof of the root cause: `r = pd.DataFrame({'A':[1.,2.,3.],'B':[np.nan]*3}).dropna(how='all').ffill().pct_change().iloc[-1]`; `r.get('B', 0.0)` -> nan (vs `r.get('MISSING', 0.0)` -> 0.0).
findings.fix: Apply the same NaN guard the helper already uses at line 359 to the P&L line: `r = todays_ret.get(t, 0.0); day_ret = sum(w * (0.0 if pd.isna(r) else float(r)) ...)`, i.e. treat an unobservable return as 0 for the day. Additionally, make the 350-353 fail-closed path shed (or stop accruing against) any held ticker whose return is not finite, so 'fail closed' means 'hold flat', not 'hold a NaN'. Optionally assert `math.isfinite(net)` before `s["equity"] *= (1 + net)` so a future NaN source fails the run loudly instead of silently corrupting the ledger.

findings.title: The band is measured against sig_fixed_weight's renormalised output, so a one-day data gap in a non-cash sleeve reads as a ~20pp breach and forces a full round trip of that sleeve

findings.what_breaks: `fixed_weight_next` compares the drifted weights to `target`, and `target` is whatever `sig_fixed_weight` returned -- which at lines 329-331 DROPS any ticker absent/NaN in the panel and renormalises the rest to gross 1.0. The guard at line 350 fails closed only for the CASH sleeve ('rather than silently going 100% risk'); the other three sleeves have no guard at all, even though dropping one changes the hypothesis actually being tested. `fetch_prices()` does `px.dropna(how="all").ffill()` — that drops all-NaN ROWS, never an all-NaN COLUMN, and ffill cannot fill a column that never had a value. So a ticker that was valid yesterday and comes back all-NaN today (a failed/renamed/delisted symbol inside a multi-ticker `yf.download` — the shield profile's own `candidate_tickers_note` says all four ETFs are still UNVERIFIED candidates) is still in yesterday's `s["positions"]` while `rets.loc[sel][t]` is NaN. `todays_ret.get(t, 0.0)` returns that NaN, not the default.

A clean day afterwards does not recover (nan*(1+r) = nan). `save_state` uses bare `json.dump`, so ledger.json is written containing `["2026-10-09", NaN, NaN]` — a bare `NaN` token that is NOT valid strict JSON and fails any JS `JSON.parse` of the raw ledger. The `/2.0` compounds it in the other direction: trend_long_flat rotates both legs on one rebalance weekday, so sale-days ~= trade-days, not trade-days/2. Net: a large, unbounded overstatement sitting in a column labelled post-tax expectancy, next to a 30% tax rate it dwarfs. Display-only and the crypto profile is enabled:false today, which caps severity -- but this is the number meant to tell Het whether class B clears its bar.

findings.title: post_tax_expectancy_vda() does not implement the per-financial-year no-loss-set-off rule the signed B1 hypothesis names it as implementing — it reports the design doc's own worked counterexample as profitable
findings.what_breaks: docs/capital_engine/hypotheses/B1_crypto_trend.md:45-47 commits to "1% TDS on every sale as a cash drag, 30% tax on realised gains with no loss offset, computed per Indian financial year in `post_tax_expectancy_vda()`", and docs/capital_engine/00_DESIGN.md:138-141 says "...*no loss set-off*... A strategy that wins 55% of trades at 1:1 is profitable pre-tax and *loses* post-tax under no-offset. Hence only slow, low-turnover... hypotheses are admissible for B, and the class's own `post_tax_expectancy` models the no-offset rule per financial year." The code is `taxed = (mean_daily_return * (1 - STCG_RATE) if mean_daily_return > 0 else mean_daily_return)`. It applies the sign test to the AGGREGATE mean, which has already netted every losing day against every winning day before tax; there is no financial-year grouping and no accumulation of gross gains anywhere in the function. The no-offset rule therefore cannot bind on any stream whose mean is positive, which is every stream a promotion would ever be argued from. The function's own docstring (lines 259-261) silently redefines the rule as "a non-positive mean gets no tax credit", which is self-consistent but is a different and far weaker rule than the two documents that name this function. This is not purely cosmetic: B1 §6 (lines 63-67) and 00_DESIGN §6 kill condition (g) are both pre-committed to be evaluated "post-tax", so this number decides whether class B is declared FALSIFIED.
findings.failing_input: The design doc's own example, evaluated with the crypto profile's committed constants (profiles/crypto.json: STCG_RATE 0.3, tax_model "vda_india"; factory.py:224 VDA_TDS_RATE 0.01). 55 winning days at +1% and 45 losing days at -1% over 100 days gives mean_daily_return = 0.001; post_tax_expectancy_vda(0.001, 100, 2) returns (+0.0006, "VDA30") — i.e. +6% over the period, reported as profitable post-tax. The per-FY no-offset computation the documents specify: gross gains 0.55, gross losses 0.45 (not deductible), tax = 0.30 x 0.55 = 0.165, so post-tax = 0.55 - 0.45 - 0.165 = -0.065 over the same 100 days, or -0.00065/day. The code returns the opposite sign on the exact case 00_DESIGN.md cites as the reason class B is restricted to low-turnover hypotheses.
findings.fix: Either implement the specified rule — accumulate gross gains and gross losses per Indian financial year from the contestant's `history`, tax 30% of gross gains only, deduct nothing for gross losses, then express per day — or amend 00_DESIGN.md §7 and B1 §4/§6 to state that the metric nets within the period before taxing and is therefore an upper bound on post-tax return. What cannot stand is a pre-committed kill condition pointing at a number whose sign can disagree with the rule it cites. Either direction edits a signed hypothesis document, so it needs Het; `profiles/crypto.json` is still `enabled: false`, so nothing in the live ledger is wrong today, but this must be settled before that profile is ever enabled (it is a natural companion to the already-recorded CE-3-03b follow-up, which notes the gate is still pre-tax).

findings.title: crossover_breed() ignores the categorical keys it claims the caller enforces, so mating produces a byte-identical clone of parent A — a fresh one every report round until MAX_CONTESTANTS is exhausted

The caller does not enforce that. attempt_breeding() buckets only on `(p["fn"], p.get("sector"))` (line 994) and crossover_breed only asserts `fn` and `sector` (lines 950-951); `proxy` and `leader` are never compared, and `child = dict(parent_a)` (line 952) silently takes parent A's value. Every live bucket varies at most ONE gene in PARAM_BOUNDS (verified against factory_state/ledger.json: event_drift buckets vary only `threshold`, momentum buckets only `lookback`, input_cost/cement varies nothing), so the child's params are necessarily identical to parent A or parent B. attempt_breeding() has no params-duplicate guard and never calls already_failed() — unlike propose_evolutions(), which guards both (`if new_params == params: continue`, line ~907, plus already_failed()). Three consequences: (a) the lineage record is factually false — gene_map says {'lb':'b','drop':'b'} while the child actually runs parent A's TATASTEEL.NS proxy, not parent B's BZ=F; (b) the clone is counted by report()'s `n_tests` (line 1197) as an independent test, raising multiplicity_sharpe_floor for every real contestant (252 days: n_tests 26 -> 2.8905, n_tests 31 -> 2.9454), i.e. a wrong number in the promotion gate; (c) the child name only de-dupes by name (`while child in reg: child = f"{base}_{suffix}"`), and the parents' `gen` never changes, so the SAME pair breeds a brand-new identical clone every single weekly report() — and because nothing ever deletes a registry entry, the registry walks to MAX_CONTESTANTS=40, which permanently disables spawn_children (line 522), propose_evolutions (line 914) and attempt_breeding itself. The whole self-evolution engine stops.

Add the asserts for those fields in crossover_breed to match its own docstring. Then add the duplicate guard attempt_breeding is missing: skip the pairing when `child_params` equals an existing `reg[*]` value or when `already_failed(child_params, state)` is true, exactly as propose_evolutions() already does. findings.title: sig_benchmark() takes a 100% position in a benchmark column with no data, poisoning the permanent benchmark's equity to NaN forever and silently freezing every promotion with no warning
findings.what_breaks: sig_benchmark() returns `{BENCHMARK: 1.0} if BENCHMARK in px.columns` — presence of the COLUMN, not of any data. yfinance returns an all-NaN column for a dead/renamed symbol (this repo already hit that: "TATAMOTORS.NS (real 404 on Yahoo)"), and `px.dropna(how="all").ffill()` keeps such a column because ffill cannot fill leading NaNs. update()'s P&L line 768 (`day_ret = sum(w * todays_ret.get(t, 0.0) ...)`) has no NaN guard, unlike the two places that do and document the convention: sig_fixed_weight skips tickers where `pd.isna(px[t].iloc[-1])`, and fixed_weight_next's docstring says "todays_ret: ... NaN = 0" and implements `0.0 if pd.isna(r)`. So day_ret becomes NaN, `s["equity"] *= (1 + NaN)` makes equity NaN permanently, and line 798's `max(s["peak"], NaN)` returns 1.0 (NaN > 1.0 is False) so drawdown is NaN, not a breach — nothing retires it. The benchmark carries `permanent=True`, which blocks retirement, demotion, evolution and breeding everywhere, so there is no code path back. Blast radius: benchmark_returns() hands report() a map of {date: NaN}, which is truthy and non-empty, so the `if require_beat_benchmark and not bench_map` warning at line 1199 ("NO contestant can be promoted this round... it is not a silent pass") NEVER PRINTS, while excess_return_stats() returns NaN for every contestant and promotion_check()'s `not _isnan(have)` test fails that check for all of them. The gate the warning exists to announce is now exactly a silent total block. Separately, save_state() writes a bare `NaN` token into ledger.json, which is not valid JSON: python json.load tolerates it, a strict parser such as the Trading Floor artifact's JSON.parse rejects the whole file.

In update() line 768, apply the convention fixed_weight_next already documents — treat a NaN return as 0.0 (`r = todays_ret.get(t, 0.0); r = 0.0 if pd.isna(r) else float(r)`) — and refuse to write a non-finite `net`/`equity` at all: skip the contestant for the day and print a loud warning, since a single NaN is unrecoverable once persisted. Make benchmark_returns() drop non-finite rows, and return None when nothing finite is left, so the existing fail-closed warning at line 1199 actually fires. findings.title: seed_registry_for_profile() silently seeds the full NSE-equity registry into any non-default profile that has no "registry" key, and the 26 dead contestants inflate the promotion gate's Bonferroni n_tests
findings.what_breaks: `if FACTORY_PROFILE != DEFAULT_PROFILE and "registry" in _PROFILE: return deepcopy(...)` / `return seed_registry()` — the fallback on line 514 applies to EVERY profile, not just equity_nse. A non-default profile without a "registry" key therefore inherits all 27 equity entries, and load_state()'s backfill loop (lines 583-587) writes them plus blank_stats() into that profile's own ledger at factory_state/<profile>/ledger.json. Their `sector` values (cement, infra, steel, pipes_tiles, nifty100) and hardcoded tickers do not exist in that profile's UNIVERSE, so every signal raises KeyError, which update()'s try/except swallows into `targets = {}` and a single `[warn]` line. The result is not a crash but a plausible-looking ledger full of contestants that can never trade — yet they are not retired, so they accrue days_on_rung every day and, worse, they are all counted by report()'s n_tests (line 1197, non-retired and non-permanent), which feeds multiplicity_sharpe_floor. The one real contestant in that arena is then judged against a Bonferroni floor computed for 26 simultaneous tests instead of 1. The docstring documents only the two handled cases and never states this fallback, and the profiles package already raises ProfileError for every other malformed-profile case, so failing loudly here is the established convention.
findings.failing_input: In memory: set FACTORY_PROFILE='fx_paper' and _PROFILE = {"UNIVERSE": {"fx": ["EURINR=X","USDINR=X"]}, "MACRO_PROXIES": [], "BENCHMARK": "USDINR=X", "STATE_DIR": "factory_state/fx_paper"} (a new profile JSON with no "registry" key — the shape tests/test_health_check.py already uses for its synthetic 'fx_paper'/'crypto_paper' profiles, and the shape any next profile added per docs/capital_engine/00_DESIGN.md will have until someone remembers the key). seed_registry_for_profile() returns 27 equity contestants referencing sectors ['cement','infra','nifty100','pipes_tiles','steel']. Running each through IMPLS against a two-column FX panel: event_cement_t30 -> KeyError 'ULTRACEMCO.NS', input_cost_lag -> KeyError 'TATASTEEL.NS'; 26 of 27 can never produce a signal, and all 26 count in n_tests. multiplicity_sharpe_floor(252, n_tests=1) = 1.6449 versus multiplicity_sharpe_floor(252, n_tests=26) = 2.8905 — the real contestant's promotion bar is 76% higher than the arena warrants.
findings.fix: Make the fallback explicit instead of silent: `if FACTORY_PROFILE == DEFAULT_PROFILE: return seed_registry()`, and for any other profile either require the key — `raise ProfileError(f"profile '{FACTORY_PROFILE}' must carry a 'registry' key")`, matching how profiles/__init__.py already rejects every other invalid profile — or return {} so the arena starts empty rather than populated with another asset class's hypotheses. A cheap belt-and-braces addition: have load_state() (or tools/health_check.py's check_profile_integrity) assert that every seeded entry's `sector` is a key of that profile's UNIVERSE and that each hardcoded ticker is in ALL_TICKERS, and refuse to seed otherwise.

findings.title: attempt_breeding() has no already-mated / duplicate-params guard: the same top pair re-mates every report() round, minting parameter-identical contestants that permanently consume the MAX_CONTESTANTS budget
findings.what_breaks: attempt_breeding() picks the two fittest eligible members of each (fn, sector) bucket and breeds them, but nothing marks a pair as having mated and nothing checks whether the child's parameter set already exists in the registry. propose_evolutions() retires the parent it evolves (factory.py:925-926) and screens candidates with already_failed(), so it is self-limiting; breeding is not. The two fittest parents stay eligible (rung 0, equity>1.0, trades>=10, days_on_rung>=126) indefinitely, so every weekly report() breeds them again. The collision loop at 1016-1019 does not reject the duplicate, it just renames it (`_2`, `_3`, ...). Because crossover_breed() inherits each gene from a or b at random and a bucket often differs in only one gene (the mom_* family differs only in `lookback`), the new child is frequently byte-identical in parameters to the one born the week before. Consequences: (a) the same hypothesis is counted as several distinct contestants, inflating n_tests and the arena that docs/research/Q6_breeding_overfitting.md models as "distinct hypotheses"; (b) registry keys are never deleted (retirement preserves them, see graveyard()), so len(reg) is a lifetime counter — the live ledger is already at 27 of MAX_CONTESTANTS=40 with 4 of those retired, leaving 13 slots. Once len(reg) hits 40, propose_evolutions() (factory.py:916) and spawn_children()'s add() silently stop producing anything, which means a real-money promotion (rung>=2) can no longer spawn the Law-2-sanctioned neighbour children at all — starved by duplicate crossover copies.
findings.failing_input: python3.13 -B -c with synthetic dicts, no disk access: reg={'a1':{'fn':'momentum','sector':'cement','lookback':40,'top_frac':0.34},'a2':{'fn':'momentum','sector':'cement','lookback':90,'top_frac':0.34}}; con={'a1':blank_stats() with equity=1.20,trades=20,days_on_rung=126, 'a2':blank_stats() with equity=1.10,trades=20,days_on_rung=126}; random.seed(0). Calling factory.attempt_breeding(reg, con) three times (one call per weekly report() round, parents untouched between calls) returns ['a1_x_a2_g1'], then ['a1_x_a2_g1_2'], then ['a1_x_a2_g1_3']. reg['a1_x_a2_g1_2'] == reg['a1_x_a2_g1'] == {'fn':'momentum','sector':'cement','lookback':90,'top_frac':0.34} — an exact duplicate hypothesis occupying a second registry slot. Registry grew 2 -> 5.
findings.fix: Before `reg[child] = child_params` (factory.py:1019), reject the birth if an identical parameter set already exists as a live or retired registry entry (the same numeric-key comparison already_failed() uses via _NON_NUMERIC_PARAM_KEYS), and/or record the mated pair in the child's lineage and skip a bucket whose two fittest members already have a common crossover child. Either check is additive, touches no RULES/LADDER/COST_PER_SIDE value, and matches attempt_breeding()'s docstring claim that a pair produces "an additional child" (singular).

findings.title: report() has no idempotence guard (update() has an explicit one): a second invocation charges PAPER_HOLDING_TAX_WEEKLY a second time to every paper contestant and runs another full breeding/evolution round
findings.what_breaks: update() carries a deliberate idempotence guard (factory.py:749-757, `already = {r[0] for s in con.values() ...}`) whose comment commits to the invariant "re-running must never be able to rewrite observed history", backed by bug_log.md's ledger-duplicate-trading-days entry. report() has no equivalent: no date key, no last-report marker (the live ledger's only top-level keys are `registry` and `contestants`), nothing. So every invocation re-applies a full weekly cycle: `s["equity"] *= (1 - PAPER_HOLDING_TAX_WEEKLY)` at line 1210 fires again for all 21 rung-0 non-permanent contestants, the drawdown that feeds the DEMOTE branch is then computed from the twice-taxed equity, and attempt_breeding()/propose_evolutions() run a second time (see finding 1 — up to BREEDING_MAX_NEW_PER_ROUND=3 more registry keys per extra run). save_state() persists all of it. This contradicts the constant's own committed specification: factory.py:222-241 names it PAPER_HOLDING_TAX_WEEKLY, says report()'s "weekly cycle" applies it, and anchors the 0.0013 value to "~India's risk-free rate, ~6.5%/yr, expressed weekly" while explicitly citing EXECUTION_PLAN.md Section 5(f) on why an arbitrary punitive rate would be a red flag. Charged per invocation rather than per week, that anchor no longer holds. The trigger is not hypothetical: .autonomous/SESSION_PLAYBOOK.md:277-283 lists `python3 factory.py report` in its QUICK COMMAND REFERENCE under the comment "Run the engine manually (writes locally only, pushes nothing)" — it does write the production factory_state/ledger.json, and the workflow's commit step is `git add factory_state`.
findings.failing_input: Run `python3 factory.py report` twice against the current ledger (27 contestants, 21 rung-0 non-permanent). Second run: each of those 21 contestants' equity is multiplied by 0.9987 a second time with no market day behind it, so equity/paper_pnl and the drawdown fed to the DEMOTE check are off by one full weekly tax tick, and a second breeding round fires. Verified by inspection plus a read-only recompute of the live ledger: e.g. event_steel_t22 dd -0.1036 -> -0.1048, mom_infra_lb40 dd -0.0823 -> -0.0835 on one extra run. The sharp edge is conditional, not currently armed: any contestant within one tax tick of RULES["max_drawdown"]=-0.12 is tipped into DEMOTE by the duplicate run alone, and three live contestants (mom_infra_lb40, mom_cement_lb40, mom_cement_lb90) already carry paper_failures=1, where a second failure retires them permanently.
findings.fix: Give report() the same shape of guard update() has — e.g. stamp the ledger with the date/ISO week of the last completed report and return early with a "this cycle is already recorded" notice on a repeat, exactly as update() does for a date already in history. Alternatively charge the holding tax from a stored last-charged date so it accrues per elapsed week rather than per invocation. Also correct SESSION_PLAYBOOK.md:280's "writes locally only" comment, which understates that the real ledger is mutated.

findings.title: Design §3.2's promotion-time class ceiling (PROMOTE-BLOCKED-BY-CEILING) is not implemented anywhere: report() promotes a non-equity profile's contestant onto a real-money rung with no class-ceiling check
findings.what_breaks: docs/capital_engine/00_DESIGN.md:68-70 commits to: "**Class ceilings bind at promotion time**: a promotion that would push a class over its ceiling is recorded as PROMOTE-BLOCKED-BY-CEILING and the contestant keeps paper status (new verdict string, no RULES change)." That string exists in exactly one place in the repository — the design doc line itself (`grep -rn 'PROMOTE-BLOCKED' .` returns only 00_DESIGN.md:69). report() is entirely profile- and class-blind: it computes `verdict = "PROMOTE"` from promotion_check() and then unconditionally does `s["rung"] = min(s["rung"] + 1, len(LADDER) - 1)`. RULES and LADDER are shared literals and deliberately not profile-driven (factory.py:22-28), so a class B (crypto) or class A1 (shield) contestant promotes onto the same Rs 25,000 rung-1 as equity, and report() prints `capital=f"Rs {LADDER[s['rung']]:,}"` for it. The ceiling exists only downstream and after the fact: portfolio/aggregate.py:186-202 labels the class "[OVER CEILING]" once the rung is already recorded, and portfolio/gates.py:177-196 (G3) checks it at real-capital activation — and gates.py's own G1 precondition is "a contestant at rung >= 1", i.e. exactly the state §3.2 says must never be reached. No work order owns the promotion-time rule (grep of WORK_ORDERS.md and work_orders/*.md for "ceiling" returns only the aggregator CE-2-03, gate CE-4-01 and the gated CE-X-01), so this is unimplemented rather than pending. Real money still needs Het's G4 sentence, so the harm is bounded to the ledger and the report recording a rung/capital figure the design forbids.
findings.failing_input: FACTORY_PROFILE=crypto (profiles/crypto.json, class B, ceiling 30% per portfolio/aggregate.py:31) with any contestant that clears promotion_check(). report() sets its rung 0 -> 1 and prints capital "Rs 25,000". Class B real exposure is then 25,000 of a 25,000 portfolio total = 100% of real capital against a 30% ceiling, which §3.2 says must instead be recorded as PROMOTE-BLOCKED-BY-CEILING with the contestant kept on paper. The aggregator will then print class B "100.0% of real capital vs ceiling 30%  [OVER CEILING]" after the fact, and gates.py G3 returns RED for the same reason — both reporting a state the promotion path should have refused to create.
findings.fix: Either implement §3.2 in report()'s verdict step — look up the profile's class letter, compute the post-promotion class share from portfolio.aggregate's CEILINGS (read-only, already available), and emit the PROMOTE-BLOCKED-BY-CEILING verdict while leaving rung unchanged — or amend 00_DESIGN.md §3.2 to state that the ceiling binds at activation (gates.py G3) rather than at promotion. Do not leave the committed verdict string with no implementation: as written, the doc overstates the guard.

findings.title: Crypto promotion gate uses only ONE benchmark; the committed B0 doc requires beating BOTH btc and the cash baseline
findings.what_breaks: benchmark_returns() returns the FIRST registry entry with permanent=True that has history ('for name, s in con.items(): if reg.get(name,{}).get("permanent") and s.get("history"): return {...}'), so promotion_check() can only ever apply the excess-return / multiplicity-corrected excess-Sharpe gate against ONE benchmark. profiles/crypto.json ships TWO permanent entries (crypto_btc_benchmark, fn=benchmark, and crypto_cash_baseline, fn=cash). The committed hypothesis doc docs/capital_engine/hypotheses/B0_crypto_cash_baseline.md:13-15 states verbatim: '**Role:** second benchmark for class B. A contestant promotes only if it beats BOTH `crypto_btc_benchmark` (see B1 §4) AND this, on the date-paired excess-return gate, post-tax.' That BOTH requirement is not implemented anywhere -- the cash baseline is silently dropped from the gate, so a class-B contestant can be handed PROMOTE on exactly the kind of evidence the Q5 fix exists to reject. Second defect from the same root: the selection is dict-order dependent, not fn-based. tests/test_crypto_profile.py:260 ('test_c_first_permanent_is_the_btc_benchmark') codifies today's accidental order rather than the intent, so a reordering of crypto.json's registry (or any future profile listing the cash baseline first) silently swaps which benchmark the gate uses -- proven below.
findings.failing_input: Probed with synthetic in-memory data (FACTORY_PROFILE=crypto, /usr/bin/python3.13, no network, no writes): 130 dates; btc_benchmark daily rets ~N(0.0002,0.008); cash_baseline = 0.0525/365 = 0.00014384/day; contestant = btc + alpha where alpha ~N(0.0006,0.0002) (i.e. a BTC-correlated contestant with small smooth alpha), days_on_rung=130, trades=14, dd=0.0, mean=0.000764, sharpe=1.62, n_tests=6. factory.promotion_check(s, mean, sharpe, <btc map>, 6) -> PROMOTE=True (excess mean 0.0006 >= 0.0; excess Sharpe 45.90 >= floor 3.3331). factory.promotion_check(s, mean, sharpe, <cash map>, 6) -> PROMOTE=False (excess Sharpe 1.3122 < floor 3.3331). Same contestant, same gate: promoted because the second benchmark the doc mandates is never evaluated. Order dependence: benchmark_returns(reg, con) returned the BTC series with con keyed btc-then-cash, and returned the CASH series after reordering the same dict to cash-then-btc.
findings.fix: Do not pick 'the first permanent entry'. Select by mechanism (reg[name]['fn'] == 'benchmark') so the bar can never be swapped by ledger key order, and make the excess-return gate iterate over EVERY permanent baseline the profile declares, requiring the contestant to clear excess-mean and the multiplicity-corrected excess-Sharpe floor against each (fail closed if any required baseline has no paired history). Because this changes promotion-gate behaviour it is Hard-rule territory: it needs Het's fresh in-session authorization, and the alternative resolution (amend B0's 'BOTH' sentence to match single-benchmark code) is also his call, not a session's. tests/test_crypto_profile.py:260 should assert selection by fn, not by position.

It does write. portfolio/aggregate.py:62-64 justifies its own global-only choice as 'a cross-profile read-only view' and adds 'Same choice advisors.py makes' -- but advisors' write target is profile-specific, so that rationale does not transfer.

findings.title: Crossover breeding manufactures byte-identical duplicates of existing contestants (100% of the time for the momentum and input_cost buckets)
findings.what_breaks: crossover_breed() starts from `child = dict(parent_a)` and only ever re-draws keys that are in PARAM_BOUNDS AND present in both parents. It has no check that the result differs from either parent, and attempt_breeding() buckets parents on `(p["fn"], p.get("sector"))` only (line 994) -- so the categorical fields the docstring says the caller enforces are NOT enforced. The docstring at line 937-938 states: "Categorical fields (fn, sector, leader/proxy) must already match between parents (enforced by the caller) and carry over as-is." `leader` and `proxy` are not in the bucket key, and the crypto profile's `rule` is not even in that list. Three concrete consequences, all verified by calling the real functions with synthetic ledgers: (1) momentum -- `lookback` is the only PARAM_BOUNDS gene the family has (`top_frac` is not in PARAM_BOUNDS), so 1000/1000 seeded crossovers of mom_cement_lb40 x mom_cement_lb90 returned params byte-identical to one parent. (2) input_cost -- seed_registry() puts `input_cost_lag` (proxy TATASTEEL.NS) and `input_cost_crude_cement` (proxy BZ=F) in the SAME bucket ('input_cost','cement'); both carry lb=20, drop=-0.05, so the only real difference (the cost proxy -- the whole point of the crude-oil hypothesis) is silently taken from parent_a and the child is byte-identical to input_cost_lag in all 200 seeds tried. (3) crypto profile -- all six trend_long_flat contestants share bucket ('trend_long_flat', None) because none has a `sector` key, so a donchian parent crosses with an sma parent and the child is an exact duplicate of an already-seeded contestant (e.g. crypto_trend_donchian_50). Each duplicate is a new registry key + a new non-retired contestant, so it is counted in report()'s `n_tests`, which raises multiplicity_sharpe_floor for EVERY contestant on the strength of tests that are literal copies; it pays PAPER_HOLDING_TAX_WEEKLY; it is displayed as an independent contestant; and its lineage claims mechanism="crossover" with a gene_map when nothing was actually combined.

findings.title: MAX_CONTESTANTS is enforced against cumulative registry keys (retired included), so all three birth paths silently die forever -- docs say it caps live contestants
findings.what_breaks: Retirement never deletes a registry or contestant key -- factory.py:113-114 states "never by deleting a registry key (history is preserved forever; see graveyard())" -- so `len(reg)` is monotonically non-decreasing. All three birth paths gate on `len(reg)`/`len(registry)` against MAX_CONTESTANTS=40, i.e. on the CUMULATIVE number of hypotheses ever defined, not on how many are alive. Once 40 cumulative keys exist, spawn_children() returns [], propose_evolutions() skips every candidate, and attempt_breeding() breaks immediately -- permanently and with no message. The self-evolution machinery that the module docstring advertises ("improves itself by SELECTION", "auto-breeds children") is then dead for the rest of the ~12-month evidence window, and propose_evolutions() can no longer replace a straggler at all. The committed docs consistently read MAX_CONTESTANTS as a cap on LIVE contestants: PROJECT_STUDY.md:388-390 -- "27 defined in seed_registry(), 26 actually live in ledger.json ... well under MAX_CONTESTANTS=40"; docs/research/Q5_statistical_power.md:138 tabulates "40 (MAX_CONTESTANTS) | 88.9%" in a table whose rows are concurrent competing contestants; Q6_breeding_overfitting.md:84 says breeding is "growing the arena toward MAX_CONTESTANTS = 40". The live ledger is already at 27 keys of which only 23 are live, so only 13 cumulative births remain -- and per finding 1 those 13 can all be duplicates.

findings.title: graveyard() reports days_survived from days_on_rung, which the rung-0 demotion reset wipes -- it shows only the final paper attempt, not how long the contestant lasted
findings.what_breaks: graveyard()'s docstring promises "Every retired, non-permanent contestant: what it was, why it died, how long it lasted." But report()'s rung-0 DEMOTE branch replaces the whole stats dict with `{**blank_stats(lineage=s["lineage"]), "paper_failures": s["paper_failures"]}` on every non-final paper failure, which zeroes days_on_rung AND empties history -- so after the first failure the contestant's recorded lifetime restarts and the earlier span is unrecoverable. Because retirement on the paper-failure cap requires paper_failures to reach 2, EVERY contestant that dies that way has had at least one reset, so days_survived systematically reports only the length of the last attempt. dashboard.py:543 renders this straight to Het as "{entry['days_survived']} days". (Related, same function: `cause` falls through to "retired (reason not mechanically tagged)" for a contestant retired by propose_evolutions(), even though s['evolved_out'] is a perfectly mechanical tag sitting in the same dict -- not yet materialized, since no evolved_out contestant exists in the live ledger.)

Also set an explicit retired_reason at the paper-cap and evolved-out retirement sites so cause is never "not mechanically tagged". This is a reporting/bookkeeping field only -- it feeds no verdict -- but it does touch report()'s state-writing path, so it belongs in a reviewed change on the branch, not a hand edit of the ledger.

findings.title: crossover_breed() produces a byte-identical clone of a live parent for every family currently in the registry — the duplicate-check guard propose_evolutions() has is missing
findings.line: 952-958 (crossover_breed gene loop), 1019 (reg[child] = child_params); contrast 909 (`if new_params == params: continue`)
findings.what_breaks: crossover_breed() starts from `child = dict(parent_a)` and then, for each key in PARAM_BOUNDS present in BOTH parents, copies that gene from a or b. If two bucket-mates differ in exactly ONE PARAM_BOUNDS gene, the child is necessarily byte-identical to one parent. That is the structural situation for every family in the live registry: the momentum family's only PARAM_BOUNDS gene is `lookback` (top_frac is not in PARAM_BOUNDS), so momentum crossover can NEVER produce anything new — 100% clone, by construction; every event_drift seed variant carries hold=3, so threshold is the only differing gene and the child is always one parent verbatim; input_cost/cement's two live members share lb=20 and drop=-0.05, so the child is always input_cost_lag verbatim. propose_evolutions() refuses exactly this (line 909 `if new_params == params: continue`); attempt_breeding() has no equivalent check, so it writes a new registry key + blank_stats contestant whose params already exist. Consequences, all on the evidence side: (a) a redundant copy burns one of MAX_CONTESTANTS=40 slots; (b) report()'s `n_tests` counts the clone as another independent test and feeds it to multiplicity_sharpe_floor(), so the Q5 multiplicity correction is computed over a test count that includes perfectly correlated duplicates; (c) the clone traces an identical equity curve, so a lucky parent now occupies two of the ten EVOLUTION_TOP_N / BREEDING_TOP_N slots and its luck is double-counted in the ranking and the breeding pool — the exact luck-propagation the 2026-08-30 Q6 day-gate fix was added to stop. It also contradicts the function's own stated purpose ("recombining their calibrated parameters", "produce an ADDITIONAL child") and the module docstring's "auto-breeds children with neighbouring parameters": a verbatim copy is neither a recombination nor a neighbour.

Same result for the real event_drift pair (event_cement_t30 x event_cement_t40 -> identical to t40 or t30, 4/4 seeds) and the real input_cost/cement pair (-> identical to input_cost_lag, 4/4 seeds). All three buckets exist right now in factory_state/ledger.json with >=2 live rung-0 members.
findings.fix: In attempt_breeding(), after `child_params, gene_map = crossover_breed(...)`, skip the birth when the result adds nothing new: `if any(p == child_params for p in reg.values()): continue` (and, for consistency with propose_evolutions()'s anti-repeat rule, also `if already_failed(child_params, {"registry": reg, "contestants": con}): continue` — breeding currently never consults the graveyard at all, so it can also resurrect an exact setup that already died). Note this changes live evolution dynamics, so per CLAUDE.md it needs Het's fresh, in-session authorization before merge, same as the Q6 gate did.

findings.title: attempt_breeding() buckets on (fn, sector) only, so crossover_breed()'s documented "leader/proxy must already match (enforced by the caller)" invariant does not hold — a cross-mechanism hybrid can be born with a misleading name
findings.what_breaks: crossover_breed()'s docstring states: "Categorical fields (fn, sector, leader/proxy) must already match between parents (enforced by the caller) and carry over as-is." The caller does not enforce that — `buckets.setdefault((p["fn"], p.get("sector")), [])` keys on fn and sector only, and the asserts at 950-951 check only fn and sector. `proxy` therefore mismatches silently and is taken from parent_a via `child = dict(parent_a)`. This is live-reachable today, not hypothetical: input_cost_lag (proxy TATASTEEL.NS, a steel input-cost mechanism) and input_cost_crude_cement (proxy BZ=F, an energy input-cost mechanism) are both live, both rung 0, and both land in bucket ('input_cost','cement') — confirmed by reading factory_state/ledger.json. Once their lb/drop genes diverge (propose_evolutions()'s mutate_params blends lb/drop toward the advisor bank, so divergence is a normal outcome), crossover produces a child whose MECHANISM comes from one parent and whose CALIBRATION was fitted against the other's completely different cost proxy — a hypothesis nobody ever stated, which is what Law 1 exists to prevent. The child's name compounds the damage: it is built from both parent names, so the audit trail reads `input_cost_lag_x_input_cost_crude_c_g1` while the actual params carry proxy TATASTEEL.NS, i.e. the registry, the lineage record and the graveyard all describe the child as part-crude when it never looks at crude.

findings.fix: Make the caller enforce what the docstring promises: key the buckets on the full categorical signature, e.g. `buckets.setdefault((p["fn"], p.get("sector"), p.get("leader"), p.get("proxy"), p.get("csv")), []).append(name)` (the same key set already named in _NON_NUMERIC_PARAM_KEYS), and widen crossover_breed()'s asserts to cover leader/proxy/csv so a future caller cannot reintroduce the gap. Also changes live breeding behaviour -> needs Het's fresh authorization.

findings.title: attempt_breeding() is not idempotent and report() has no re-run guard (unlike update()), so re-running report breeds more contestants and re-charges the weekly paper tax on unchanged evidence
findings.line: 1012-1022 (name-collision loop only appends a suffix, no "already bred this pair this round" check); report() 1189-1325 (no idempotence guard); 1210 (PAPER_HOLDING_TAX_WEEKLY applied per call)
findings.what_breaks: update() got an explicit idempotence guard on 2026-09-13 (lines 744-760) precisely because repeated execution double-counted history, and the workflow comment at lines 825-830 says the code guard exists so "the code guard stops the corruption from any other trigger (manual dispatch, re-run)". report() has no such guard, and attempt_breeding() is non-idempotent by construction: the only collision handling is `while child in reg: child = f"{base}_{suffix}"`, so a second invocation against unchanged parent stats mints another new registry key rather than recognising the pair already bred. Each extra report() run therefore (a) births up to BREEDING_MAX_NEW_PER_ROUND=3 further contestants from evidence that has not changed by a single day — BREEDING_MAX_NEW_PER_ROUND's comment claims it "caps a single report() round's births", which only holds if a round happens once — and (b) multiplies PAPER_HOLDING_TAX_WEEKLY (0.13%) into every rung-0 contestant's equity again, so a week with two report runs charges two weeks of holding cost and corrupts the equity ranking that breeding and evolution both select on. Reachable two ways: LOCAL_SETUP.md:40-49 tells the operator to run `python3 factory.py report` manually and states "Safe to run repeatedly while exploring" — directly contradicted by this behaviour; and a GitHub Actions "Re-run jobs" on the Sunday scheduled run preserves github.event.schedule == '30 4 * * 0', so .github/workflows/factory.yml's report step fires again against the already-committed ledger and commits the extra children to main.
findings.failing_input: reg/con as in finding 1 (two eligible momentum parents, unchanged between calls); random.seed(7); calling factory.attempt_breeding(reg, con) five times with no mutation of parent stats in between returned a new child every time: ['mom_cement_lb40_x_mom_cement_lb60_g1'], ['..._g1_2'], ['..._g1_3'], ['..._g1_4'], ['..._g1_5'] — registry grew 2 -> 7, every child a byte-identical duplicate of a parent (finding 1 compounds this).
findings.fix: Give report() the same shape of guard update() has — record the last report date in the ledger (e.g. state['last_report_date']) and skip with a printed notice if report() is invoked again for the same week, so the paper tax, the verdicts and the births happen once per round. Independently, make attempt_breeding() refuse a pair it has already bred this generation (the lineage records parents + gen, so `if any((con[k]["lineage"] or {}).get("parents") == [a, b] and (con[k]["lineage"] or {}).get("gen") == gen for k in con): continue`). And correct LOCAL_SETUP.md:49: `report` is not safe to run repeatedly against a ledger you intend to keep. Behavioural change to the weekly cycle -> needs Het's fresh authorization.

findings.title: "Best paper contestant" is picked by equity with no history requirement, so a freshly-created (equity=1.0, history=[]) contestant wins and silently blanks or corrupts the portfolio drawdown
findings.what_breaks: summarize_ledger() picks the class's representative paper contestant by `s["equity"]` alone (line 146) and returns that contestant's curve as `_curve`. factory.blank_stats() (factory.py:558-562) creates contestants with `equity=1.0, history=[]`, and report() inserts them routinely: on every paper DEMOTE reset (factory.py:1284), every spawn_children (1274), every advisor evolution (922) and every crossover (1020). Verified against the live factory_state/ledger.json: ALL 22 non-retired, non-permanent rung-0 contestants are currently below 1.0 (best = input_cost_lag at 0.99642). So the next blank_stats() insertion is strictly the highest-equity paper contestant, becomes `best`, and contributes an EMPTY curve. blend_curves() then drops that class entirely. Single-class (today): paper_view.max_drawdown -> None, points 0, classes_blended [], table prints "no overlapping paper history to blend", risk_manager prints "max DD n/a" -- the drawdown monitor blinds itself precisely when the whole arena is underwater. Multi-class (once crypto/shield ledgers exist): the class is silently dropped and the OTHER class's drawdown is published as "the portfolio drawdown" -- a plausible-but-wrong number, not an error. Separately, the per-profile table and the dashboard/Artifact JSON report best_paper_equity = 1.0000 for a contestant that has never traded. No test covers this: every contestant in tests/test_portfolio_aggregate.py has a non-empty history.

Better still for the drawdown number: blend all live paper contestants in the class rather than cherry-picking the single highest-equity one, which also removes the winner-selection bias. Add a test with a zero-history contestant present.

findings.title: blend_curves() intersects dates, so sessions a weekend-trading class has and an equity class lacks are discarded -- a class B weekend crash is erased from the portfolio drawdown
findings.what_breaks: The paper-view blend keeps only dates common to every class present. profiles/crypto.json commits `"trades_weekends": true` while profiles/equity_nse.json has `"trades_weekends": false`, so class B's Saturday/Sunday rows (and equity-market holidays generally) are thrown away rather than carried forward. Drawdown is a path statistic: dropping the observations where the trough occurs does not shrink the window slightly, it deletes the drawdown. The module docstring calls the result "the portfolio drawdown" and 00_DESIGN.md s3.3 pre-commits -10%/-15% portfolio drawdown rules "evaluated by portfolio/"; this is the only drawdown the package computes, and it is the number agents/risk_manager/risk_manager.py:107 and tools/build_trading_floor_state.py:192 publish to the dashboard/Artifact. The CE-2-03 evidence packet flags only that "the blend window shrinks to their overlap" -- it does not record that a weekend-trading class's extreme moves become invisible.

Class B (trades_weekends) 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 0.60 (Sat 07-04), 0.62 (Sun 07-05), 0.99 (Mon), 0.99. agg.max_drawdown on class B alone = -0.40.
