findings.title: Advisor Sharpe/robustness use an all-walk-days denominator while the promotion gate uses in-market days only — inverts the ranking inside every bank bucket
findings.what_breaks: `backtest()` appends a net return for EVERY day of the walk (advisors.py:107 is unconditional), so out-of-market days enter the series as 0.0. `sharpe_advisor` (:128) and `robustness_advisor` (:129) therefore divide by the full walk length. factory.py:801-804 only accumulates `sum_ret`/`sum_sq`/`days_in_market` when `s["positions"]` is non-empty, and factory.py:1211-1217 computes the gate Sharpe as `sum_ret/days_in_market` — in-market days only. The advisor's number is the gate's number scaled by ~sqrt(days_in_market/walk_days), so it is not merely a different scale: because the scale factor varies across candidates in the SAME bucket (`threshold` and `drop` are exactly the knobs that change in-market frequency), the within-bucket ordering flips. The advisor layer is ranking on a metric the tournament never uses, and 2 of the 3 heuristics carry the bias. This contradicts advisors.py:76-81 ("Walk the full history exactly like update() does") and the committed design record maintenance_notes/2026-08-23_advisor_layer.md:12-14, which states the layer runs "through the *same* sig_* functions factory.py runs live (no separate/divergent backtest logic)". It also defeats factory.py:145-148's own claim that MIN_SHARPE_SAMPLE_DAYS=20 is the "same guard advisors.py's own sharpe() uses": advisors.py:115 tests `len(returns) < 20` against the walk length, so a candidate in market on only 2 of 870 days still returns a finite, bank-eligible Sharpe, whereas factory.py:1213 would return NaN.

Sweeping the live grid's own event_drift thresholds (0.02..0.08, hold=2) through advisors.backtest() and scoring the IDENTICAL net series two ways — full series vs. only days where positions were non-empty at the top of the iteration (same costs, only the denominator differs):
  thr=0.02  advisors.sharpe= 6.77   in-market-denominator= 11.03   in-mkt 466/870
  thr=0.08  advisors.sharpe= 2.55   in-market-denominator= 24.26   in-mkt  34/870
advisors.ensemble_rank() therefore writes threshold=0.02 as picks[0] (ensemble_rank 2.67), while factory's own promotion Sharpe ranks threshold=0.08 first (24.6 vs 11.0) — a full inversion along the threshold axis. The live committed factory_state/parameter_bank.json shows the predicted bias direction: event_drift/cement and event_drift/infra both rank the grid's near-lowest threshold (0.03) at ensemble_rank 1.0.
findings.fix: Score the in-market subset, so advisors.py and factory.py agree on one definition of the Sharpe denominator. Have `backtest()` also return the per-day in-market mask (`bool(positions)` evaluated before `positions = targets`, matching factory.py:801), have `score_candidate()` compute sharpe/robustness on `net_returns[mask]`, and apply the `len < 20` guard to the in-market count so it actually mirrors MIN_SHARPE_SAMPLE_DAYS. One reconciliation decision has to be made explicitly while doing this: factory.py:801 evaluates `if s["positions"]` on YESTERDAY's positions, so the entry-day net — which carries the full entry cost, ~0.59% of NAV at LADDER[1] on a 6-name basket — is excluded from `sum_ret`/`sum_sq` entirely. Whichever convention is chosen, both files must use it, and the committed bank should be regenerated afterwards since its current scores and orderings were produced under the diverged one.

findings.title: A missing/empty price column publishes a whole bank bucket of -99.0 sentinels, and propose_evolutions() retires a live paper contestant on the strength of it
findings.what_breaks: `sharpe()` returns the sentinel -99.0 for "not enough data" (:116) and "zero variance" (:119). `train()`'s only viability filter is `if net.empty: continue` (:164), which is True only when `len(px) <= warmup` — a candidate that never traded for 5 straight years produces an 870-long all-zero series, so it is NOT empty and goes straight into the bucket. Nothing downstream rejects the sentinel: `ensemble_rank()` ranks it as an ordinary number, the bank is written with it, and factory.py:904-907 takes `picks[0]["params"]` with no quality check at all, then retires the live parent (`retired=True`, `evolved_out=True`). Nothing warns, either: the `n_errors` print at advisors.py:109-111 — added by the committed fix bug_log.md `backtest-silent-exceptions` — only fires when a sig fn RAISES, and `sig_event_drift`/`sig_input_cost` return `{}` on missing data rather than raising. The consequence is the inverse of the project's purpose: a contestant carrying 126+ days of irreplaceable real paper evidence is destroyed and replaced by a child whose recorded justification is literally `sharpe: -99.0`. Partial yfinance failures across the ~110-ticker ALL_TICKERS list, and NSE symbol renames, are the realistic trigger; BZ=F is also in the panel.
findings.fix: Three independent guards, any one of which stops this. (1) In `train()`, drop a candidate whose `sharpe == -99.0` or whose `n_trades == 0` instead of banking it, and skip writing a bucket that has no survivors — a bucket with no tradeable candidate should be absent from the bank, which factory.py:905 already handles correctly via `if not picks: continue`. (2) Have `backtest()` warn on zero trades across the whole walk, since the existing `n_errors` warning structurally cannot see a sig fn that returns `{}`. (3) In `fetch_history()`, raise on any all-NaN column among the tickers the grid actually references (leaders, proxies and every UNIVERSE[sector] member) rather than ffill-ing silence into the walk. Separately, factory.py:907 should require a minimum score on `picks[0]` before retiring a live contestant — note the currently committed bank already has negative-on-all-three top picks (momentum/cement sharpe -0.075, robustness -1.002, cost_efficiency -0.4508; momentum/pipes_tiles -0.17 / -0.752 / -1.6971), so that path already fires toward measured losers without any sentinel involved.

findings.title: Bank buckets are keyed (family, sector) but omit the proxy/leader ticker that drives the signal, so input_cost params fit on TATASTEEL.NS are transplanted onto the BZ=F (Brent) contestants
findings.what_breaks: `sig_input_cost` is driven entirely by `px[p['proxy']]` (factory.py:286-292), so a fitted `lb`/`drop` pair is only meaningful for the proxy it was fitted against. `build_grid()` generates input_cost candidates for exactly one proxy — `for sector, proxy in [('cement', 'TATASTEEL.NS')]` (:62) — but `buckets.setdefault((fn, sector), ...)` (:167) and `bank.setdefault(fn, {})[sector]` (:172) key the output on sector alone, discarding the proxy from the lookup path while leaving it inside the stored `params` dict. factory.py:904 then resolves `bank.get('input_cost', {}).get('cement')` for ANY cement input_cost contestant, and `mutate_params` blends only the numeric keys while its own docstring states "Categorical fields (fn, sector, leader, proxy) are never changed". The live registry has three input_cost entries across two different proxies (factory.py:486-497), so a Brent-driven contestant gets its drawdown threshold retuned using evidence gathered from steel prices — a plausible-looking number with no evidentiary basis for that signal. This also contradicts the committed design record (maintenance_notes/2026-08-23_advisor_layer.md:14-15: grids "stay inside the same mechanism-bounded ranges the seed registry already uses"), since the registry's BZ=F proxy instances are never in the grid at all. Two silent coverage gaps follow from the same key: `input_cost_crude_steel` (sector=steel) and `mom_nifty100_lb90` (sector=nifty100) have no bucket, so they can never be evolved and nothing reports that.
findings.fix: Key the bucket on the full categorical signature of the signal, not just the sector: build it as `(fn, sector, params.get('proxy') or params.get('leader'))` at advisors.py:167, nest the proxy/leader level into the written bank at :172, and have factory.py:904 look up with that same signature so a contestant with no matching bucket gets `picks = None` and is correctly left alone instead of retuned off the wrong price series. Then extend `build_grid()` to cover the (sector, proxy) pairs the registry actually holds — ('cement','BZ=F') and ('steel','BZ=F') — so the two crude contestants have real evidence of their own rather than inheriting steel's. A cheap interim guard with no restructuring: in propose_evolutions, skip the pick when any of (`proxy`, `leader`) differs between `params` and `picks[0]['params']`.

findings.title: _directive_lines() never ends the NEEDS HET section in the real het_directives.md, so G4 is blind to every authorization written at the file's actual append point — and G3 then sizes its ceiling check with Rs 25,000 instead of the authorized amount, turning a true RED into GREEN
findings.line: 136-151 (_directive_lines), consumed at 190 (`amount = auth[2] if auth else ladder[1]`)
findings.what_breaks:
`_directive_lines()` sets `in_needs = "NEEDS HET" in line` on every line starting with `#`, so the NEEDS HET region runs from its heading to the next heading of ANY level. `.autonomous/het_directives.md` contains exactly two headings — line 1 and `## NEEDS HET` at line 79 — and the file is append-only, so every dated entry from 2026-10-03 onward (lines 138-144, including Het's real granted directives such as line 139's A2 grant) sits BELOW that heading. Measured on the committed file: 52 lines start with `- 20`, only 45 are returned, and the newest eligible line is dated 2026-08-29. Two consequences. (a) G4 can never read GREEN from a real grant: it prints "G4 awaiting owner: no dated 'AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A <contestant> <amount>' line in het_directives.md (a human must write it, in session)" when the line is in fact present, which contradicts CE-4-01's committed spec ("The evaluator checks presence") and would push a session to re-ask Het or hand-edit the log. (b) Worse, because `find_authorization()` returns None, `gate_g3` silently falls back to `ladder[1]` = Rs 25,000 and checks the class ceiling against an amount the owner never authorized — so the one gate that is supposed to bind the authorized rupee amount to the class ceiling evaluates a fictional, far smaller number and reports GREEN where the real amount is over the ceiling. tests/test_gates.py:171 only ever exercises the happy case `"## NEEDS HET

## Log

" + AUTH_A`, i.e. a synthetic file that does have a following heading; no test runs the parser against the committed het_directives.md.
findings.failing_input: Probe 1 (real committed file, builtins.open patched to serve the real text so nothing is written): `gates._directive_lines(ROOT)` -> 45 lines, last date 2026-08-29, while the text holds 52 `- 20` lines. Appending the grant exactly as the log appends one — `- 2026-10-11 | "Authorize real capital for the shield" | **GRANTED = §6 A6: AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A mom_nifty100_lb90 500000**` — still gives `find_authorization(ROOT,"A") -> None` and `gate_g4 -> AMBER ... no dated 'AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A ...' line`. Probe 2 (synthetic aggregate view in memory: class A holds Rs 10,00,000 real, class B Rs 0, ladder = factory.LADDER): with the authorization visible, `gate_g3(root,"B",LADDER,("2026-10-11","btc_trend_lb200",1_000_000))` -> ('RED', 'class B would hold 50% of real capital after activating Rs 1,000,000 (authorized amount), ceiling 30%'); with it invisible via this bug, `gate_g3(root,"B",LADDER,None)` -> ('GREEN', 'class B 2% of real capital after Rs 25,000 (rung-1 amount) <= ceiling 30%').
findings.fix: Stop inferring the section boundary from "the next heading of any level" when the section is the last one in the file. Two changes: (1) in `_directive_lines`, close `in_needs` only at a heading of equal-or-shallower level than the NEEDS HET heading, and — because no such heading exists today — delimit the region explicitly (e.g. an `<!-- /NEEDS HET -->` marker the file writers maintain, or select on bullet shape: NEEDS HET items never start with `- 20`, chronological entries always do). (2) Add a regression test that runs `_directive_lines()` against the committed `.autonomous/het_directives.md` and asserts the newest `- 20` line in the file is present in the result, so the parser can never again silently drop the live append region. Until that lands, `gate_g3` should refuse to invent an amount: when `auth` is None it is evaluating a hypothetical, and the reason string should say so rather than reporting GREEN against `ladder[1]`.

findings.title: The 'example'/'e.g.' suppression in find_authorization() runs AFTER backtick and strikethrough spans are stripped, so an explicitly-labelled example line reads as a genuine owner authorization and G4 goes GREEN
findings.what_breaks: `find_authorization()` does `clean = re.sub(r"~~.*?~~", " ", line)`, then `clean = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", " ", clean)`, and only then `if re.search(r"example|e\.g\.", clean, re.I): continue`. The example/e.g. guard is therefore applied to text from which backticked and struck spans have already been deleted — so whenever the words "example" or "e.g." are themselves inside a `backtick` or `~~strike~~` span (an extremely common way to mark a word in this repo's own Markdown: see het_directives.md line 95's `` `ENABLE PROFILE <shield_nse|crypto> WITH RULES AS PROPOSED` `` and the `~~...~~`-marks-resolved convention used throughout lines 85-135), the marker vanishes and the surrounding, unbackticked AUTHORIZE sentence matches `_AUTH_RE` and is accepted as a dated owner authorization. G4 then returns GREEN — on the one gate whose entire purpose is to represent a fresh, specific, human consent to deploy real money. tests/test_gates.py:174-175 cover only the inverse cases (sentence inside backticks, plain "for example" outside any span), both of which correctly give AMBER, so the ordering bug is untested.
findings.failing_input: `- 2026-10-11 | reminder, the sentence Het must write is AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_a 25000 (`example` only, nothing granted)` -> after stripping, `clean` reads "... AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_a 25000 (  only, nothing granted)", the example guard does not fire, and `_AUTH_RE` matches -> G4 GREEN. Same for `- 2026-10-11 | ~~for example~~ AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_a 25000` -> GREEN. Both verified: `suppressed_as_example=False, reads_as_authorization=True`.
findings.fix: Evaluate the example/e.g. guard on the RAW line before any span stripping (move the `re.search(r"example|e\.g\.", line, re.I): continue` check above the two `re.sub` calls), and keep the span stripping only for the `_AUTH_RE` match. A line that mentions "example" anywhere, in any markup, must never be read as consent — failing closed costs nothing here because G4's absent state is AMBER, not RED. Add the two inputs above as regression tests next to test_quoted_example_ignored.

findings.title: No contestant identity is ever bound across G1, G2 and G4, so a class can read all-five-GREEN assembled from three different contestants — including a retired one and one that does not exist in any ledger
findings.line: 226-229 (evaluate_class), with gate_g2 at 113-133 and find_authorization at 154-173
findings.what_breaks: CE-4-01's committed gate definitions are per-contestant: G1 is "≥ 1 contestant PROMOTED by promotion_check() to rung 1", G2 is "a file `docs/capital_engine/validation/<class>_<contestant>_<date>.md` ... re-deriving the verdict", G4 is "`AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL <class> <contestant> <amount>`", and 00_DESIGN.md §8 A6 unlocks "Real capital for one contestant in one class". The evaluator never joins them. `gate_g2` globs on `f.startswith(letter + "_")` only and is not even passed a contestant name; `gate_g1` returns the qualifying name buried in a reason string; `find_authorization` does return the authorized name, but `evaluate_class` hands `auth` only to `gate_g3` (for its rupee amount) and otherwise discards `auth[1]`. Nothing checks that the authorized contestant exists, is non-retired, is the one that cleared G1, or is the one the validation file is about. The composed output then reads "all five gates met (a human still acts)" for a class where no single contestant has evidence + independent validation + owner authorization — a plausible-but-wrong GREEN at the exact point the design relies on the evaluator so that "a RED can never be argued away".
findings.failing_input: Synthetic probe (in-memory, os.listdir/os.path.isdir/open patched; nothing written): validation dir containing only `A_monsoon_cement_2026-01-05.md` -> `gate_g2(root,"A")` = ('GREEN', 'validation file present and dated: A_monsoon_cement_2026-01-05.md'), although `monsoon_cement` is `retired: True, rung: 0` in the committed factory_state/ledger.json and so can never be the G1 contestant. Directive text `- 2026-10-11 | Het: AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_that_does_not_exist 25000` -> `gate_g4(root,"A")` = ('GREEN', 'dated line 2026-10-11: AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_that_does_not_exist 25,000') and `find_authorization` = ('2026-10-11','strat_that_does_not_exist',25000), a name absent from every ledger. With G1 GREEN from a third contestant (e.g. mom_nifty100_lb90) and G5 GREEN, evaluate_class returns verdict GREEN, reason 'all five gates met'.
findings.fix: Thread one contestant through the class evaluation. Have `gate_g1` return the qualifying contestant name as structured data (not only inside its reason text), pass the G4 contestant into `gate_g1` and `gate_g2`, and require: the G4 name exists in a ledger of that class and is non-retired/non-permanent; the G1 qualifying contestant IS the G4 name; and the G2 filename parses as `<class>_<contestant>_<date>.md` with `<contestant>` equal to the G4 name. When the names disagree, report RED on the mismatching gate with both names in the reason, rather than GREEN. Add a test asserting that a validation file and an authorization naming different contestants cannot together produce a GREEN class.

findings.title: format_table prints "kill tripped: no" as a literal; the -15% KILL rule can never be displayed, and gate_g3 fails OPEN on it
findings.what_breaks:
Two linked defects in the one pre-committed portfolio kill condition (00_DESIGN.md s3.3: "-15% -> everything to A1's liquid ETF and the KILL file is written ... (pre-committed, evaluated by portfolio/)").

(a) format_table() never reads view['drawdown_rules']['kill_tripped']. Line 260 ends with the hardcoded string `kill tripped: no`. The sibling field `status` on the same line IS read from the dict, so the renderer looks dynamic but the kill flag is a constant. tests/test_gates.py:120 does `view["drawdown_rules"]["kill_tripped"] = True` to drive G3 RED, which proves the flag is meant to be dynamic -- so this is not a harmless "it's always False anyway": the only human-facing rendering of the portfolio view is wired to a constant and will keep printing "kill tripped: no" after the flag starts being computed. tests/test_portfolio_aggregate.py:106 only asserts the flag is False, so nothing catches it.

(b) aggregate() line 231 returns `kill_tripped=False` unconditionally, and gates.py:185 `if dr["kill_tripped"]:` treats that as PASS. gates.py's own docstring (line 16) advertises G3 as checking "aggregator kill rule not tripped AND the class's share ...". An un-evaluated condition therefore fails OPEN on a gate to real capital, which is the opposite of every other guard in this repo (kill switch, malformed ledger -> RED, G1/G2 unmet -> RED). DD_KILL_RULE (-0.15) and DD_PAPER_RULE (-0.10) are defined, printed, and never compared to anything; paper_view.max_drawdown is computed and never tested against them. EVIDENCE/CE-4-01.md:49 discloses "always False today", but nothing in the code is conditional on "today", and the format_table half is disclosed nowhere.
findings.failing_input:
(a) Display bug, reproducible against the real committed ledger with no real capital needed:
$ python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/home/user/strategy-factory')

v = agg.aggregate(ladder=[0,25000,50000,100000,200000])

(b) Fail-open gate, synthetic root (temp dir, two profiles class A2 + B1, LADDER=[0,25000,50000,100000,200000]): class A holds one rung-2 contestant (Rs 50,000 real) plus a paper contestant with history equity [1.0, 2.0, 0.8]; class B one paper contestant with the same curve.
agg.aggregate(tmp, ladder=LADDER) -> paper_view['max_drawdown'] = -0.6, drawdown_rules = {'paper_trigger': -0.1, 'kill_trigger': -0.15, 'status': 'real-money drawdown not tracked yet -- evaluate manually', 'kill_tripped': False}
G.gate_g3(tmp, 'A', ladder=LADDER) -> ('GREEN', 'kill rule not tripped; class A 100% of real capital after Rs 25,000 (rung-1 amount) <= ceiling 100%')
A -60% blended drawdown with real capital deployed, and the gate reports "kill rule not tripped".
findings.fix: In format_table, replace the literal with the flag: `f"...; kill tripped: {'YES' if dr['kill_tripped'] else 'no'}"`. In gate_g3, fail closed on an unevaluated rule: if aggregate reports no real-money peak tracking (status != a computed figure), return RED/AMBER with "G3 unmet: portfolio drawdown rule not evaluable (no real-money peak tracking)" instead of reading a literal False as a pass. Either compute kill_tripped from a tracked real-money peak, or return kill_tripped=None so a truthiness test cannot silently mean "safe".

findings.title: Real exposure under a class letter outside A/B/C (including a missing "class" key) inflates total_real_exposure but belongs to no class, understating every class share and flipping gate G3 from RED to GREEN
findings.line: 159 (class_letter), 184 (total_real), 186 (for letter, ceil in CEILINGS.items()); consumed at portfolio/gates.py:191
findings.what_breaks:
`class_letter` is just `str(prof.get("class", "?"))[:1].upper()`, and the per-class loop iterates only over CEILINGS = {A, B, C}. A profile whose class letter is anything else -- a typo, a future sleeve, or simply a profile with no `class` key at all (which yields "?") -- still has its rung>=1 exposure summed into `total_real_exposure` at line 184, but is a member of no class at line 187. Nothing validates the key: profiles/__init__.py only checks FORBIDDEN_EQUITY_KEYS, and tests/test_profiles.py:127 happily uses `**{"class": "T"}`. No entry is added to `problems`, so gates.py:183's "aggregator reports problems -> RED" does not fire either.

The module docstring asserts the invariant "ceilings: B 0.30 and C 0.20 are MAXIMA of TOTAL real capital". That invariant breaks: share = class_exposure / total_real uses a denominator containing capital that belongs to no class, so every class's share is understated by exactly the unmapped amount, and gate_g3's ceiling check (line 191) inherits the same inflated denominator. The result is a real-capital ceiling guard that can be defeated by a single unrecognised `class` string in a JSON file.

findings.title: The "equal-weight" paper-view blend averages un-rebased equity levels, so the portfolio drawdown is weighted by each class's equity level at the window start, not equally
findings.what_breaks:
blend_curves returns `sum(c[d] for c in curves) / len(curves)` over the raw equity levels. That is only an equal-weight blend if every curve equals the same value on the first common date. Over the intersection window the curves start at whatever level each has reached, so the implied starting weights are level_i / sum(levels) -- the older, higher-compounded class dominates.

This contradicts the committed description of the number in two places: the module docstring says the curves are "blended with equal weight (mean of equity levels)", and EVIDENCE/CE-2-03.md's ASSUMPTIONS says "Equal-weight blend = mean of equity levels (buy-and-hold of equal starting weights)". Mean of un-rebased levels is buy-and-hold with starting weights proportional to each class's current equity, not equal starting weights. The work order (.autonomous/capital_engine/work_orders/CE-2-03.md:5) asked for something different again: "combined equity curve weighted by ceilings for the paper view".

This is the single number compared against the pre-committed -10% / -15% portfolio thresholds (00_DESIGN.md s3.3), printed by format_table and republished by agents/risk_manager and tools/build_trading_floor_state.py. The error is latent today only because one class (A) has a ledger, so the blend is a single curve; it activates the moment a second class's ledger exists.
findings.failing_input:
Two class curves on the same three dates, fed straight to the shipped functions:
  A = {"d1": 1.80, "d2": 1.80, "d3": 1.80}   # class A, flat, 3 years of compounding behind it
  B = {"d1": 1.00, "d2": 0.70, "d3": 1.00}   # class B, newly started, -30% then recovers
  agg.max_drawdown(v for _, v in agg.blend_curves([A, B]))  -> -0.107143  (-10.71%)
Rebasing each curve to 1.0 at the first common date first (true equal starting weights, as documented):
  -> -0.150000  (-15.00%)
The reported -10.71% sits below the pre-committed -15% KILL level while the blend the docstring describes is exactly at it. A starker case: A = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0], B = [10.0, 5.0, 10.0] -> code reports -45.45% (implied starting weights 9.1% / 90.9%) where the equal-weight blend is -25.00%.
findings.fix: Rebase each class curve to 1.0 on the first common date before averaging (`c[d] / c[first_date]`), which is what "equal starting weights" means, or implement the ceiling-weighted blend the work order specified; then correct the docstring and the "equal-weight blend" wording in format_table to match whichever is chosen. Add a unit test with two curves at different starting levels -- the existing tests only blend curves that both start at 1.0, so the bug is invisible to them.

findings.title: Class verdict can read GREEN with the evidence (G1), validation (G2) and owner authorization (G4) belonging to three different contestants — the authorized contestant is never checked to exist, be live, or be at rung >= 1
findings.line: 225-233 (evaluate_class; `auth` is computed at line 226 and passed ONLY to gate_g3), 80-110 (gate_g1), 112-133 (gate_g2)
findings.what_breaks: `evaluate_class` resolves the authorization (`auth = find_authorization(...)`, line 226) and then hands it to `gate_g3` alone, purely to pick the rupee amount. `gate_g1` and `gate_g2` never receive it: G1 goes GREEN on ANY non-permanent, non-retired contestant in the class at rung >= 1 with enough days_on_rung, and G2 goes GREEN on ANY `validation/<letter>_*.md` that names a date. Nothing anywhere verifies that the contestant Het named in the `AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL` line exists in a ledger of that class, is non-retired, or has itself ever been promoted. This contradicts committed spec: design §6 requires "a fresh, dated, **specific** `AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL <class> <contestant> <amount>` line" and §8 A6 grants "Real capital for **one contestant** in one class"; the CE-4-01 work order says "fresh, in-session, specific"; EXECUTION_ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md §5 check #2 states the gate answer is "**contestant** has a dated `AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL` line and gate state not RED" with source "`CE-4-01` evaluator" — a per-contestant question the evaluator cannot answer. The damage surface is the human-facing output: `summary_lines()` (what `tools/build_trading_floor_state.py` line 198 feeds to the Trading Floor Artifact Het reads) collapses to the bare string "GREEN -- all five gates met (a human still acts)" with no contestant name at all, so the green light appears to endorse funding a contestant that has zero rung-1 evidence. `tests/test_gates.py` never catches this because `make_tree()` uses the name `strat_a` in the ledger, the validation filename and the directive line simultaneously.
findings.failing_input: Ledger for class A: `{"registry": {"strat_x": {}, "strat_a": {}}, "contestants": {"strat_x": {rung:1, days_on_rung:130, retired:false, ...}, "strat_a": {rung:0, days_on_rung:400, retired:true, ...}}}`; validation file `docs/capital_engine/validation/A_strat_a_2026-10-08.md`; directive line `- 2026-10-09 | Het: AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_a 25000 | **GRANTED**`. The authorized contestant strat_a is retired and has never been above rung 0.
findings.fix: Thread `auth` into G1 and G2 and make the contestant the subject of the gate: when an authorization exists, G1 must be RED unless THAT contestant is present in a ledger of THAT class, non-permanent, non-retired, at rung >= 1 and days_on_rung >= min_days; G2 must require a validation file whose name (or body) matches that contestant, not just the class letter. findings.title: G4 (owner authorization) matches the AUTHORIZE pattern anywhere in a directive line and ignores negation and the line's own status field, so a DECLINED / pending / "do NOT" log entry reads GREEN
findings.line: 154-172 (find_authorization; the only exclusions are `~~strike~~`, `` `backticks` `` and the regex at line 168 `example|e\.g\.`), 53 (_AUTH_RE)
findings.what_breaks: `.autonomous/het_directives.md` is written BY sessions, not by Het, and its own committed format (that file, line 11) is `` `DATE | directive (summarized) | status` `` — existing entries carry statuses like `**DECLINED**`, `**CORRECTED, NOT BUILT**`, `**ACKNOWLEDGED, GUARDRAILS UNCHANGED**`, `**PENDING**`. `find_authorization` parses the pattern out of the middle of the line and never looks at the status field or at any negation. So the normal, well-intentioned act of logging a capital request that was refused, deferred, or merely explained turns the owner-authorization gate GREEN. The author clearly anticipated non-authorizing mentions — hence the strikethrough, backtick and `example|e.g.` filters and the deliberate exclusion of the `## NEEDS HET` section where pending items live — but those filters cover only three phrasings, and the CE-4-01 evidence packet asserts "G4 is conservative", which this contradicts. G4 is the one gate whose entire purpose is to prove a human said yes; combined with G1/G2 eventually going GREEN on real evidence, a prose log line alone flips the class to GREEN with no authorization ever given.
findings.failing_input: Any of these single lines as `.autonomous/het_directives.md` content (outside NEEDS HET), today=2026-10-10 — each returns `('GREEN', 'dated line 2026-10-09: AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_a 25,000')` from `gate_g4`, verified by probe: (a) `- 2026-10-09 | Het asked about AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_a 25000 | **DECLINED**`; (b) `- 2026-10-09 | do NOT AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_a 25000 until validation lands | **PENDING**`; (c) `- 2026-10-09 | to fund it he must write AUTHORIZE REAL CAPITAL A strat_a 25000 himself | **NOT YET WRITTEN**`.
findings.fix: Fail closed on anything but an unambiguous grant: require the match to start the directive body (i.e. the text immediately after the `DATE |` separator, so the sentence is the directive rather than a mention inside prose) AND require an explicit grant marker in the status field (e.g. `GRANTED`), AND reject the line if the cleaned text contains a negation/deferral token (`not`, `never`, `declin`, `pending`, `awaiting`, `revok`, `withdraw`, `must write`, `would`, `if he`, `proposed`). An ambiguous line should yield AMBER (awaiting owner), never GREEN — AMBER is already the never-RED resting state of this gate, so failing closed costs nothing.

findings.title: No gate reads the global KILL file, and G3's only kill check is a flag the aggregator hardcodes to False — so the gate report still prints GREEN while the engine is frozen
findings.line: 185 (gate_g3 reads `dr["kill_tripped"]`), 209-222 (gate_g5 checks only that the TEXT `def kill_switch_active(` appears in factory.py); see also /home/user/strategy-factory/portfolio/aggregate.py:231 `kill_tripped=False`
findings.what_breaks: `factory_state/KILL` is the project's emergency stop: every write path honours it (factory.py:706, factory.py:1185, and aggregate.py's `--write` as of 2026-10-11), and design §3.3 says a -15% real-money drawdown writes it, while §6 kill condition (i) says a broker/ledger reconciliation mismatch writes it. The gate evaluator — the pre-flight checklist a human consults before deploying capital — never looks at that file on any path. The one kill-shaped check it has, `dr["kill_tripped"]` in G3, reads a key that `aggregate()` sets to the literal `False` at line 231 and never computes, even when `total_real_exposure > 0`; the existing test `test_g3_flips_on_kill_rule` only passes by monkeypatching `agg.aggregate` to inject `True`, which confirms the production branch is unreachable. G5 checks the kill switch by regex-matching a `def` line in factory.py source, so a present-but-gutted function passes (the test tree's own factory.py is literally `def kill_switch_active(...): return None`). Net effect: with class A's gate ceiling at 1.0 the share check is trivially satisfiable, so G3 for the one class that gets funded first has no reachable failure mode except an unreadable ledger, and a KILL-frozen repo reports "Class A: GREEN -- all five gates met". That contradicts design §6's G5 ("kill switch **live**, reconciliation designed") and the module docstring's "RED anywhere = no real money" framing. (The always-False flag is disclosed in `.autonomous/capital_engine/EVIDENCE/CE-4-01.md` RISKS; the absence of any KILL-file check is not disclosed anywhere.)
findings.failing_input: Take the exact synthetic tree from `tests/test_gates.py::make_tree` (baseline asserts A and B all-GREEN), add one file `factory_state/KILL` containing `recon mismatch 2026-10-11` — the design §6(i) condition that must stop all money — then run `G.evaluate(root, ladder=LADDER, min_days=126, today=TODAY)`: output is unchanged, `verdict == "GREEN"` for A and B, every gate GREEN. Confirmed statically: `grep -n kill portfolio/gates.py` shows the only runtime use is `dr["kill_tripped"]` (line 185) and a regex over factory.py source (line 213); `grep -rn _kill_switch_active portfolio/` shows it is called only from aggregate.py's `--write` path, never from `aggregate()` itself.
findings.fix: Add an explicit kill check to G5 (or a new pre-gate): if `factory_state/KILL` exists at `root`, or `<class profile state dir>/KILL` exists for any profile of the class, return RED with the file's reason text — fail closed and anchored at `root`, the way `aggregate._kill_switch_active()` already does. Separately, either make `aggregate()` compute `kill_tripped` from the real-money peak once `total_real_exposure > 0`, or have `gate_g3` stop advertising "kill rule not tripped" in its GREEN reason string while the flag is a constant, so the report does not claim a check it is not performing.

findings.title: check_duplicate_dates is pinned to "info" for the live equity profile with no baseline, so a recurrence of the ledger-duplicate-trading-days bug keeps the 15-minute supervisor green
findings.what_breaks: For `profile == DEFAULT_PROFILE` the check always returns `[("info", ...)]`, no matter how many duplicates there are or what dates they fall on. `main()` then takes `if all(level == "info" for level, _ in results): return 0`, and supervisor.yml's only signal is `python tools/health_check.py --profile "$P" --live || FAILED=1`. Probing `run_all()` on the real checkout shows the complete current finding set is exactly two INFO rows (duplicates + phantom days) -> exit 0. So the monitor is permanently incapable of going red on new duplicate history rows -- the exact defect it watches for, measured in factory.py's own comment at 142 extra rows across 26 of 27 contestants and "a ~19% overstatement of every contestant's progress toward the 126-day promotion bar". The discriminator needed is already computed and then discarded: all 146 live duplicates fall on dates <= 2026-09-11 (2026-07-10 x11, 07-14 x11, 07-17 x11, 07-31 x11, 08-07 x11, 08-14 x13, 08-21 x14, 08-28 x20, 09-04 x21, 09-11 x23), i.e. every one predates the 2026-09-13 idempotence guard (695ddac), so any duplicate on a later date is unambiguously a live regression and is reported identically to the frozen historical noise.
findings.failing_input: Real factory_state/ledger.json with one brand-new duplicate row appended: `h = led['contestants']['nifty_benchmark']['history']; h.append(list(h[-1]))` (re-records 2026-10-06, a post-guard date). Baseline: `[('info', '[equity_nse] 146 duplicate history row(s) across 24 contestant(s)... Known historical duplicates; cleanup is the owner's call, nothing to fix here.')]`. After injection: identical except `147`. Level stays "info", so `main()`'s all-info branch returns 0 and supervisor.yml stays green.
findings.fix: Keep the historical set as INFO but escalate on recency: `check_duplicate_dates` already builds per-date counts, so emit a WARNING when any duplicated date is newer than the guard's cutoff (or newer than a recorded baseline/max-known-duplicate date) and keep INFO only for dates at or before it.

findings.title: check_stale_ledger's "4 calendar days behind the last weekday" test stays silent through 4 consecutive missed daily updates / 6 calendar days, and it is now the only staleness guard the supervisor workflow runs
findings.line: 125-129 (_last_weekday_on_or_before), 176-182 (age > 4 test); tools/supervisor_check.py:36,70-73 (the 3-day ERROR no longer wired)
findings.what_breaks: The staleness measure is calendar days between the last recorded date and the last *weekday on or before today*, not missed trading sessions, so Sat/Sun rollback freezes `ref` at Friday and widens the silent window instead of narrowing it. supervisor.yml:60 runs only `health_check.py`; `tools/supervisor_check.py`'s `check_pipeline_staleness` (STALE_DAYS_THRESHOLD = 3 counted from today, ERROR-level) is no longer invoked anywhere in CI, so the stricter test was dropped, not superseded. The docstring claims the tolerance is calibrated so that "a long weekend is tolerated, a dead cron is not"; a cron dead for four consecutive sessions is in fact tolerated. The checked-out ledger is in this blind spot right now: last date 2026-10-06 (Tue) with today 2026-10-11 -- health_check is SILENT (exit 0, green), while supervisor_check on the same data returns `('error', 'last trading update was 2026-10-06, 5 days ago ... The daily factory.yml run may have stopped firing.')`. RUNBOOKS.md:269 still routes this symptom to "Verify `supervisor.yml` runs `supervisor_check.py --live`. If it does not, that's the bug - escalate", which the workflow no longer satisfies, so the triage table misfires on the one alarm supervisor_check.py's docstring calls "the one thing worth a real red X: the automation quietly stopped".
findings.failing_input: `check_stale_ledger('equity_nse', ledger_data={'contestants': {'x': {'history': [['2026-10-05', 0.0, 1.0]]}}}, today=d)` with last recorded Monday 2026-10-05 returns `[]` (SILENT, exit 0) for every d from 2026-10-06 through 2026-10-11 -- Tue/Wed/Thu/Fri sessions all missed, six calendar days of a dead pipeline -- and only warns on 2026-10-12 (age 7). Same call with the live `last=2026-10-06, today=2026-10-11` is also SILENT.
findings.fix: Measure missed *sessions*, not calendar lag off the last weekday: count weekdays strictly between the last recorded date and today and warn at >=2 (a single holiday stays tolerated), or re-wire supervisor.yml to also run `supervisor_check.py --live` so its 3-day ERROR still covers the headline case; either way update RUNBOOKS.md:269's row to the check that actually runs.

findings.title: check_phantom_days returns "info" although its own docstring specifies "warning", so a new phantom day cannot turn the supervisor red
findings.what_breaks: The docstring states: "INFORMATION ONLY: returns a single 'warning' (never an error) naming the dates." The code at line 377 returns `[("info", ...)]`. The severity word is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `main()` exits 0 iff every finding is "info" (lines 529-531) and supervisor.yml keys solely on exit status, so the shipped check can never make the run red while the documented one would. That matters because the CE-0-04 guard in factory.py only landed 2026-10-04 (20a3b93) and runs on live yfinance data this sandbox cannot reach; if the guard regresses or a new ffill pattern slips past `unchanged.iloc[-1] >= PHANTOM_UNCHANGED_FRACTION`, the resulting phantom day advances `days_on_rung` and lowers the sqrt(252/n) multiplicity Sharpe floor (both toward easier promotion, per detect_phantom_days.py's header) while the monitor reports it as context and exits 0.
findings.failing_input: The real factory_state/market_log.json already contains six 100%-unchanged days (2026-08-27, 08-31, 09-14, 09-28, 10-01, 10-02). `check_phantom_days(log_data=<that log>, macro=['BZ=F'])` returns level "info"; `run_all()` on the checkout yields only these two INFO rows and `main()`'s all-info branch returns 0. Appending any new post-guard phantom date to that dict changes only the count inside the same INFO string.
findings.fix: Return the level the docstring specifies -- "warning" for any phantom date newer than the 2026-10-04 guard commit, "info" for the frozen pre-guard set -- so a post-guard occurrence fails the run while the historical record stays non-blocking.
